parts.text: # Ticket status ledger

Status values: `todo` → `planned` or `questions` → `ready` → `in-progress` → `review` → `done`, or `blocked` (PROCESS.md section 13). Complexity: `low`, `medium` or `high` from the plan (PROCESS.md section 4); it picks the test-author and builder models. Phase 0 ratings were set by the orchestrator on 2026-10-18 from the v1 plans (no planner rating existed); the planner re-rates a plan it re-validates.

Only the orchestrator edits this file (enforced by hook). It records each stage's result: planner → `planned`/`questions`; Stage 2 → `ready`; build → `in-progress`, `review`; reviewers' verdict → `done` (with commit) or back to `in-progress`; three failed reviews or a question for Josh → `blocked`.

A ticket starts only when every ticket in its `depends_on` (in `tickets.json`, base IDs already expanded) is `done`. The Depends on column here is the original text, for reading only. Notes also records the models used for each dispatch and why (PROCESS.md section 4). Notes holds plan deviations (what the merged code does differently from its plan; dependents' plans are re-validated against it) and `needs-josh-confirm` wording (user-visible text no plan covered, listed in the phase PR for Josh). Pick tickets with `node vault/tools/next_ticket.mjs`; validate with `--check` (done needs a commit hash, blocked needs a note, statuses must be known, STATUS.md and tickets.json must list the same tickets).

# Questions ledger: open and escalated

Three files, one ledger (Josh 2026-10-28): `QUESTIONS.md` holds open and escalated questions (new questions are added there); `QUESTIONS-answered.md` holds answered questions the build still needs; `QUESTIONS-archive.md` holds answered questions it no longer needs (every ticket named is done and no unfinished plan or phase file cites them). Rows move only whole and unchanged, by `node vault/tools/next_ticket.mjs --sort-questions` (rule in that file). Look a Q-ID up in all three files.

Chain of command: asking agent → orchestrator → specialist (calc-auditor / security-reviewer / code-reviewer) → Josh. No citation, no answer. Business and product decisions always go to Josh. Full rules: `vault/PROCESS.md`, Stage 2.

Statuses: `open`, `answered-agent`, `escalated` (waiting on Josh), `answered-josh`, `confirmed-josh` (an agent answer Josh confirmed). Agent answers not yet confirmed when Stage 3 starts stand as written.

IDs never change or get reused. Josh's answers are also appended to the decisions file for the spec area (`vault/spec/decisions/<area>.md`; index in `vault/spec/decisions/INDEX.md`). Until Oct 18, 2026 they went to `vault/spec/decisions.md`, now split into that folder.

questions.question: 11 Budgets says "a frame every 16 ms on desktop (60 fps) and every 33 ms on the iPad (30 fps); no frame over 100 ms", but no source says which statistic of the measured frame intervals must meet the 16 / 33 ms part (frames on a 60 Hz screen arrive in steps of 16.7 ms, so a frame that just makes 30 fps measures 33.3 ms, and timer jitter adds about 1 ms); the options are (a) the 95th-percentile frame interval is at most 1000/30 ms (iPad) or 1000/60 ms (desktop) plus 1 ms for timer jitter, with no frame over 100 ms (planner's recommendation; EZD-017, EZD-207 and EZD-1701 should then use the same rule), (b) the average frame rate over the measured passes is at least 30 fps (iPad) or 60 fps (desktop), with no frame over 100 ms, or (c) every measured frame is at most 1000/30 or 1000/60 ms plus 1 ms.
questions.answer: (a): the 95th-percentile frame interval is at most budget + 1 ms (1000/30 iPad, 1000/60 desktop), and no frame over 100 ms. EZD-017, EZD-207 and EZD-1701 reuse this rule. Josh can override.
questions.source: 11 Budgets; decisions P1 (budgets and rules by Claude)

questions.question: No source sets the security parameters of the contract. Options: (a) accept the planner's values: every request EZ Draft sends (API calls and webhooks) is signed with HMAC-SHA256 over `<t>.<METHOD>.<path and query>.<body>` with the tenant's signing secret, plus an `EZDraft-Tenant` header; EZ Binder learns the tenant id from a signed `connection.check` delivery at Connect (no fourth value beyond R32's three); timestamp tolerance 300 seconds; signing secret and inbound key at least 32 random bytes; sign-on codes at least 128 bits (22 base64url characters), matching EZD-1705's share-token floor; (b) the security-reviewer sets different values or a different scheme, and T11, T12 and T13 follow it.
questions.answer: (a) with three changes: the HMAC-SHA256 signed string includes the tenant (`<t>.<EZDraft-Tenant>.<METHOD>.<path and query>.<raw body>`) and EZ Binder binds the tenant at `connection.check` only after the signature verifies and the header equals the body; signing secret and inbound key are 32 CSPRNG bytes (43 base64url chars) and Connect refuses shorter; EZ Draft issues 256-bit sign-on codes (contract floor stays 128 bits), stored hashed, single use. Tolerance 300 s accepted. Josh can override.
questions.source: 11 Security; 07 Delivery rules; R32; R15; 03 rule 11; R26 R14; phase-17 EZD-1705

questions.question: EZD-006 leaves `project` writable by signed-in users through the REST API, EZD-009's `enqueue_job` is callable over REST, and EZD-018 puts the access token in browser memory, so a member can write rows or enqueue jobs directly without the server's can() permission check. Which mechanism closes this, and which ticket owns it? Options: (i) revoke direct table writes and write through security-definer functions that check the permission; (ii) a PostgREST pre-request hook; (iii) a separate database role for server routes.
questions.answer: (ii): a PostgREST pre-request gate. Server requests carry a server-only secret header; `private.api_request_gate()` (registered as `pgrst.db_pre_request`) refuses every anon/authenticated PostgREST request without a matching header (allow-list: anon `rpc/health`); fails closed. RLS stays the independent backstop. EZD-006 owns it in phase 0; EZD-007's `createSessionClient()` sends the header from a server-only env name; EZD-133 adds a direct-PostgREST money-column refusal test; EZD-132 must keep Storage policies tight. Josh generates the secret for each cloud project and Vercel (runbook). Josh can override.

questions.question: Josh wants automation wherever possible. Who runs a production release? Options: (a) automatic on merge: a GitHub Actions workflow, triggered when Josh merges the phase PR into main, backs up the production database, applies migrations and makes the new build live, stopping (live site unchanged) on any failure; production keys live in a GitHub environment no agent can read; (b) an agent runs the release from Josh's PC (needs production keys in agent reach, against CLAUDE.md rule 12); (c) keep the manual promote script Josh runs.
questions.answer: (a): releases are automatic when Josh merges the phase PR into main. A GitHub Actions workflow takes the database backup, applies migrations and makes the build live; any failure stops it and the live site stays on the previous version. Production secrets live only in a GitHub environment restricted to main; agents never see them. Josh's merge is the only approval. Replaces EZD-023b's Josh-run promote script; the agent deny on local release commands stays as a safety net.

questions.answer: Opus 5.5 by default, Fable on retry: test-author and builder run Opus 5.5 on high tickets and reach Fable 5.1 only as the escalation step after a behavior, requirement or test FAIL on Opus; code-reviewer always Opus 5.5; security-reviewer Fable 5.1 on high tickets; phase-auditor Fable unchanged. Applied in fix mode from the C2 session's 765d1cd (which had made Opus the ceiling) plus the retry ceiling restored. Check after about 5 high builds (optimize plan C8); if review rounds rise, move test-author back to Fable first.

questions.question: Supabase's public Auth API (not behind the server-only API gate) still answers 403 to a code request for an address with no account, so someone calling it directly can tell which emails have accounts; EZD-007d's own sign-in action hides this. Accept it as a known risk for v1 with Supabase's rate limits as the only control (recommended: it needs a script against the Auth endpoint and reveals only whether an email is invited), or add a sign-in captcha (Supabase Auth supports hCaptcha/Turnstile; a new ticket and account)?
questions.answer: (b): add a captcha to sign-in (Josh: "b"). New ticket EZD-034 (phase 0), built and tested with the provider's test keys; provider and account: Q-0241.

questions.question: What is EZ Draft for, and what is held for v2?
questions.answer: EZ Draft makes a clean, measured plan the crew can build from, plus a permit set when needed; it helps clients decide on selections with AI photoreal renders of the exact items; any layout can be built or changed. Every feature is built for v1; nothing is held for v2.

questions.question: Who may start a project, measure and draw?
questions.answer: Any staff member, including crew-level, can start a project. Measuring and drawing are not tied to one person: anyone starts, anyone finishes, in any order; any staff member may be sent mid-job to re-measure or add measurements. Fully customizable permissions decide who can do what, changeable at any time.

questions.question: Add plumbing and mechanical drawings to v1?
questions.answer: Yes. v1 adds plumbing sheets (supply and drain locations, plumbing diagrams such as riser or isometric, plumbing calculations if the department needs them), mechanical sheets and calculations, and a tile layout sheet that needs client sign-off. Plumbing and mechanical rules and calculations are researched before Round 3 and checked there.

questions.question: Should EZ Draft check that the drawings match the scope of work?
questions.answer: Yes, for every department. Example (Boca Raton rejection): the scope listed electrical the client had removed and the drawings had no electrical. Scope and drawings must agree both ways. Rule details in Round 3.

questions.question: When is a load calculation needed, and where do the common loads come from?
questions.answer: Load calculation for a panel change, a service change or new circuits. Common loads are data: every new account gets a default set, and the user can add new ones and edit existing ones in Settings. Values in Round 3.

questions.question: Engineer, architect and structural work?
questions.answer: A seal box is always available on permit drawings. Minor structural items (for example moving a wall) can be drawn; EZ Draft builds no structural calculations.

questions.question: Disclaimer in the terms only, or on screen too?
questions.answer: On screen as well as in the terms, on basically every page, along the lines of: "This is for design and planning purposes. These calculations and codes must be confirmed by the user and a licensed person within the jurisdiction." Exact wording and placement in Round 2.

questions.question: Are security, performance, accessibility and screen states a late hardening phase?
questions.answer: No. The proper architecture comes from the start: each slice meets and tests the security, performance, accessibility and screen-state rules for what it builds. Backups, the terms page and the on-screen disclaimer move to the first slices; slices 52 and 53 keep only the final whole-app checks and code-rule verification.

questions.question: Are the newer boards the mockups for screens still labelled "not in mockup"? (prep C1-C4)
questions.answer: Yes. Boards S01b, S15b, S17c and S19-S22 are the mockups; the "not in mockup" labels come off where the board shows the control.

questions.question: New project wizard: dialog or full page, and which fields? (prep C3, C16)
questions.answer: A dialog over the Projects page, as board S01b shows. It adds a Scope of work field (R28) and a Foreman picker (R31).

questions.question: May a crew sign-in link be shown on screen? (prep C11)
questions.answer: The person sending an invite gets a link they can send to make sign-in easy for staff. The everyday sign-in email link is still never shown on screen (Q-0035).

questions.question: Lock release and share-link expiry: fixed or settings? (prep C12)
questions.answer: Settings, starting at 5 minutes and 30 days.

questions.question: Ways to start a project? (prep C13)
questions.answer: Six: Polycam scan, PDF, DXF, supplier kitchen PDF, field measure, blank.

questions.question: EZ Binder connection and change orders in v1?
questions.answer: No EZ Binder connection in v1; the connector is built later together with the EZ Binder side (BACKLOG.md). Projects and clients are entered in EZ Draft. EZ Draft offers a downloadable "Scope PDF" (written scope plus before/after drawings or renders, from any revision or design option) that Josh attaches to an estimate or change order in EZ Binder.

questions.question: Closeout?
questions.answer: A simple workflow with no blockers and nothing the system detects: a "Mark complete" action for anyone with permission; the project moves to a Completed filter on Projects, stays viewable and can be reopened.

questions.question: Must every added product go into the catalog?
questions.answer: No. When adding a product the user can choose not to add it to the catalog, since many items are one-off uses.

questions.question: Which building departments first?
questions.answer: Build and test first: unincorporated Palm Beach County, Boca Raton, West Palm Beach. Research in Round 4: North Palm Beach, Delray Beach, Boynton Beach, Lake Worth Beach, Wellington, Riviera Beach. The Broward presets (Broward County, Fort Lauderdale, Coral Springs) stay as options.

questions.question: Phase list and order? (prep C7)
questions.answer: The 53 slices are the phase list, with the moves recorded in PHASES.md (Round 1 approval). Work is broken down within each phase; tickets and specs carry enough that an agent need not read other files, and stay short. 3D and renders are built in order with no wait for a real job; the build runs 24/7.

questions.question: May gaps the stories did not touch wait for their round?
questions.answer: Yes: screens in Round 2, calculations and the plumbing and mechanical research in Round 3, outside services and departments in Round 4.

questions.question: Is pricing removed from v1 along with EZ Binder?
questions.answer: No (answer a): pricing stays in EZ Draft as the spec has it (catalog prices, render allowance, cost and sell-price permissions). Only the EZ Binder hand-off goes.

Test changes recorded in the plan: T5 workers 4 (Q-0114 already says so) and a new T5 assertion that the web server env sets SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY to empty (EZD-007f security-reviewer minor, handoff 2026-10-20).

questions.answer: Split applied: three parts, status todo, in the phase file, tickets.json (ACs from gen_acs.mjs) and STATUS.md in one commit; EZD-016a is itself the last part and depends on both, so its dependents keep depends_on. questions.question: Project status: who moves it?
questions.answer: Moved by hand (Draft, Client review, Permit submitted, Approved, In build, Complete); only Complete has its own button (Q-0191).
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Revisions after permit submittal and after approval?
questions.answer: After Permit submitted, permit drawings can be revised. Every area changed since the last issued set gets a cloud with the revision triangle automatically; a change that is undone loses its cloud; clouds can also be added or removed by hand. Nothing locks after approval: pages, details, specs, selections and renderings can be added at any time, including during In build (selections are often finalized after approval); changes after an issue go into the next revision.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Delete vs Archive?
questions.answer: Delete is offered at any time, even after a send, and removes everything permanently after the user types the project name; the client link stops working and storage is freed at once. Archive is also offered: it hides the project behind an Archived filter, keeps everything and can be restored.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Permissions for rename, status, upload, cancel import; Foreman and Crew "own jobs"?
questions.answer: Rename, Set status, upload into a project and cancel an import are allowed to anyone who can edit that project (no separate switches). "Own jobs" are the projects a user is listed on; picking someone as a project's Foreman lists them on it automatically.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Wizard failure paths and required fields?
questions.answer: If Create fails the dialog stays open with everything typed and shows a Try again message. An unreadable file or a PDF with no known scale never blocks: the project is created with the file attached and a banner; the scale can be added later. The department (submittal) profile is never required.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Field measure that never comes back?
questions.answer: The project shows "Waiting for field measurements", who it was sent to and a Resend button; it never expires. The sender or anyone who can edit the project can cancel it.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Bearing wall removal: blocked or flagged?
questions.answer: Allowed with a warning that it needs an engineer; the warning stays on the issue checklist until "engineer letter on file" is ticked.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Lock auto-release when the holder's save failed?
questions.answer: The holder's unsaved changes stay on their device as a draft and they are told; the lock still releases.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Dimension precision and room area rounding?
questions.answer: Measurements are stored to 1/16". Wall and room dimensions show to the nearest 1/2"; cabinet and detail dimensions to 1/16"; both changeable in Settings. Room areas print in whole square feet. (Worked examples in Round 3.)
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Disclaimer wording and placement?
questions.answer: Wording (Josh): "For design and planning only. All calculations and codes must be verified by the user and a licensed professional in the project's jurisdiction." Shown on every screen; not printed on sheets.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Acknowledgment at print, export and issue?
questions.answer: Before every PDF export and every permit issue the user ticks: "I understand EZ Draft does not guarantee code compliance or acceptance by any building department. All responsibility for these drawings and calculations is mine." Name and time are saved in the project history.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Who sees which Settings pages?
questions.answer: One permission switch per Settings page (Users, Company, Title block, Departments, Defaults, Catalog, Render models, Code edition, Libraries, Translations), so the owner chooses exactly who sees what.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: System status page?
questions.answer: Owner only. Shows the last backup, failed background jobs and render usage.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: What can a client do on the share link?
questions.answer: View, comment, choose between design options, approve and sign.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: What does the Share panel hold?
questions.answer: Link on or off, who it was sent to, expiry date, Copy link, Resend.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Shared screen-state rules?
questions.answer: Empty list: one short line plus the main button (for example "No projects yet" with New project). Failed load: inline message with Retry, never a blank screen. No permission: controls are hidden, not greyed; a page opened without access says "You don't have access to this. Ask your supervisor." Office editor offline: banner "Offline. Changes are saved on this device and will sync." and work continues.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Import review persistence and Cancel?
questions.answer: Detected items are saved until Finish or Cancel, even if the browser closes. Cancel returns to the project with nothing imported.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Invite flow and who sees the code?
questions.answer: The invite email goes out; the person who sent it and the owner see the copyable invite link and the invite's 6-digit code (for now, until emails reliably reach inboxes). The invitee enters the code and lands on Projects; invites expire in 7 days (Q-0050). Everyday sign-in codes and links are never shown to anyone else. Security-reviewer checks the implementation.
questions.source: Round 2 interview, in chat (vault/questions/interview-plan-2026-10-20.md Round 2; prep gaps vault/questions/interview-00-prep.md section 1)

questions.question: Anything from the mockup chat not yet in the spec?
questions.answer: Nothing beyond what the mockup boards already show.

questions.question: When the whole database hangs, EZD-169's awaited report waits on `record_error_alert` on that same database. `/api/health` then does not answer at its 3,000 ms limit, and Q-0285 (a) leaves only about 1 s before the release check aborts at 4,000 ms. Options: (a) the health route registers the report with `after()`, so the 500 goes out at the limit and the Sentry event follows. This plan is written for (a), which is recommended; it reverses EZD-169's "await, not after()" for this one route and edits EZD-169 T5. (b) Keep the await and cap it at a set wait, which needs a number below about 1,000 ms. (c) Keep EZD-169's await and test only a stalled health RPC, so a hung database still gets no timely 500.
questions.answer: (a) the health route registers the report with `after()` (try `after(report)`, catch `void report()`), so the 500 goes out at the 3,000 ms limit and the Sentry event follows; the other three EZD-169 routes keep `await`. (b) needs a wait no source gives; (c) leaves the hung-database path unfixed (Q-0268).

questions.question: The public tunnel `app/src/app/api/monitoring/route.ts:88-89` copies the envelope header `event_id` to Sentry as sent, without a check. After EZD-142, `scrubEvent` keeps the event's own `event_id` only when it matches its `EVENT_ID` pattern (`app/src/lib/errors/scrub.ts:295`). So a caller of the public tunnel can still put any text, an email address for example, into the header that reaches Sentry (11 Security and audit; Q-0268: no known issue is parked). EZD-142's plan leaves `route.ts` alone because EZD-143 edits it in the same phase. Proposed: add to EZD-143's scope and plan that the tunnel forwards the header `event_id` only when it matches the same pattern (else it omits it), with a test. The other option is a separate phase 1 fix ticket.
questions.answer: Separate phase 1 fix ticket EZD-183 (depends on EZD-142, which defines `EVENT_ID` in `scrub.ts`, and EZD-143, which edits `route.ts`): the tunnel forwards the envelope header `event_id` only when it matches the same pattern, with tests; omit or refuse is the planner's choice with a citation; security review. Not widening EZD-143: rate limits per caller are a separate concern from the header value, and its ready plan would need re-planning (Q-0316 (a), Q-0283 (a) precedent).

questions.question: `unit-steps.mjs merge` (lines 143-144) runs `git worktree remove` and `git branch -D` without checking their exit status. Three findings are still open, each fully specified: (1) security: the new escape guard ignores quoted names, so `set "standard_conforming_strings" = off` or `"set_config"(…)` can switch string decoding off and a later plain string can create a table the check does not see (proven on the local database); fix: treat a quoted name like a plain word, plus 4 test rows; refusing every backslash instead would break the real repo's migrations (EZD-023a T16); (2) one corpus case (E10 TL3) has no test row; (3) a docs cell says T1-T8 where it should say T1-T10. Options: (a) allow one more round (R5): the planner first checks every word-only comparison in the new rules and decides, with a probe on PostgreSQL 17.11, whether a quoted name can stand in for it, so the next round closes the whole class; then tests, build and both reviews again (recommended); (b) waive the zero-findings merge rule and merge round 3 as it is, with a phase 1 fix ticket for finding (1). The check would ship with a known security gap until that ticket merges (not recommended).

questions.question: Each company gets a storage limit, and users are regularly prompted to delete older data. What is the limit, what happens when a company reaches it, and how often are users prompted?
questions.answer: One cap for all of a company's stored data: 100 GB. Every office user is reminded at 80%, 90% and 100%. At 100% the company is blocked from storing more; files already stored can still be opened, exported and sent (R-032 Option B behaviour, limit and reminders as Josh set them). Sent files are no longer permanent (reverses R24 #4a and 11 Data retention "Sent versions ... are permanent"): a company may download them, delete them for good, or keep them on EZ Draft within its limit; this needs a ticket that removes the sent-file lock (`sent_files_soft_delete`, EZD-025) and updates the spec, numbered when the storage-limit work is planned. The Supabase spend cap is decided at launch, when the production project is created (Q-0113).
questions.source: Tabled by Josh (2026-10-19), not answered: research first (storage cost per GB at the providers, average storage used per project) before the limit, the at-limit behaviour and the prompt frequency are set. Research: vault/research/R-032.md.

questions.question: Charging other companies for EZ Draft: which payment provider (for example Stripe), which plans and prices, and is there a free trial? Needed before phase 53 is planned, not before.
questions.answer: Stripe (Billing and Tax). $50 a month per company, 5 office users included, unlimited field and crew users, $10 a month per extra office user. Free trial: 14 days, no card, no AI renders. Renders: an included monthly allowance capped at $3 of render cost per company; unused allowance rolls over one month only; renders past the allowance are charged $1 per fast render and $5 per photoreal render; each render allows one free redo if it does not turn out well. How the allowance, rollover, redo and extra charges are tracked and shown to users is still to be designed (Josh 2026-10-28); open detail: whether the redo applies to included and extra renders alike and whether a redo counts toward the $3 cap.

questions.question: Render credits for paying companies (follows Q-0237): how render use, the $3 cost cap, rollover, redo and extra charges are tracked and shown.
questions.answer: Render credits replace dollars for paying companies (supersedes Round 24 #18 and S15f decision 2 for them): 100 credits a month per company; fast 1, standard 2, photoreal 5 credits; extra credits $1 each (so $1 fast, $2 standard, $5 photoreal); unused credits roll over one month then expire, oldest used first. The $3 cap is on real provider cost: when a company's included renders reach $3 of cost in a month before its credits run out, included renders stop and extras begin. Redo: an extra (paid) render gets one free redo with the same input and settings; a redo of an included render uses credits. Shown: the tier picker shows credits per tier and the balance; an extra render needs a confirm ("This render is extra: $N on your next bill") every time; after an extra render a Redo button (free once); Settings Render models shows credits used, carried over and left, and extras this month in dollars; office users are reminded at 80% and 100% of credits used; provider cost is shown only to the operator. Tracked in an append-only credit record (grant, rollover, use, redo, extra, expiry) linked to the render with its real cost; extras go to Stripe as metered usage keyed by render id. Trial: renders blocked with a notice. Worth Properties (tenant 1) is never limited by credits or company billing: no credit balance, no extra charges, no subscription (Josh 2026-10-28).

questions.question: `requestSignIn` hides the hook's 403 and every 429 except `over_request_rate_limit` (Q-0174 (a)). The plan does not say what any other Auth error (a 500, a network failure) does. The builder throws `sign_in_request_failed` (a 500, per docs/architecture.md Errors and logging "500 unexpected", "nothing fails silently"); since an email-send failure can only happen for a known address, that answer differs from an unknown address's. questions.answer: Keep the 500. Q-0174 (a) hides only answers an attacker can trigger at will (hook 403, resend 429); a 5xx or network failure is not, and a hook or database outage fails unknown addresses the same way. The one asymmetric case (a send outage for a known address) leaks nothing beyond the public Auth endpoint already escalated as Q-0175, while `{ step: 'code' }` on a failed send would leave the person with no email and no error. Josh may override with Q-0175.

questions.question: EZD-153 (the release safety check must catch tables and functions created in text it cannot read) failed its extra round 3 (Q-0331 (a)), so it is blocked again. Every earlier finding is closed: both reviewers confirmed the quoted-name gap (Q-0331), the missing E10 TL3 test row and the docs range are fixed, the gate is green and Production-sensitive changes PASS. But the security-reviewer found two new ways through, and the code-reviewer one minor: (1) security: the scanner treats letters outside plain ASCII (`é`, a non-breaking space) as punctuation, while PostgreSQL reads them as part of a name, so `select 1 as é$t$ into x from (select 1) as x$t$` hides a table create from every rule; (2) security: inside a PL/pgSQL body the scanner skips the `select … into` rule, but `for r in explain analyze select … into t loop` and `return query explain analyze select … into t` create the table; (3) minor: the `checkWithoutTag` comment lists three reasons, the code has four (`string_escape`). Scanner side checked by the orchestrator this session: both spellings give no finding, the plain control gives `hidden_create`; that PostgreSQL 17.11 really creates the tables is the security-reviewer's own probe. This is the fourth round where each fix closed every named case and the reviewer found a new spelling the hand-written reader sees differently from PostgreSQL (comments, E-strings, quoted names, now non-ASCII names and EXPLAIN): the approach of listing spellings is not converging. Counts on the 45 migrations on develop (orchestrator, this session): 0 non-ASCII or control characters anywhere, 0 uses of `explain`. Options: (a) one more round (R6) that refuses instead of listing: any character outside printable ASCII, tab and line breaks outside a comment, string, quoted name or body is refused, `explain` in any body is refused, the dollar-tag rule is matched to PostgreSQL, the comment is fixed, new test rows; costs nothing on today's migrations (counts above), but a fifth kind of gap could still turn up (recommended); (b) change the design: apply the new migrations to a scratch database and compare the objects really created with what the scan found, so the database is the reader and the whole kind of gap closes; a larger re-plan, because `lint` and the release would need a database; (c) waive the zero-findings rule and merge the round 3 code as it is, with a phase 1 fix ticket for (1)-(3); it is stricter than develop everywhere, but ships with two known gaps until the fix merges (you declined this once, Q-0331).
questions.answered_by: Josh (2026-10-27: "334- sounds like b is a better long term decision. again, i want this system to be robust, bug free, and secure.")
questions.answer: (b): change the design. The new migrations run on a scratch database and the objects really created are compared with what the scan found, so the database is the reader and the whole kind of gap closes. questions.question: EZD-316 (GitHub login only through one script) is built (round 3: 59/59 tests, builder's gate green; not yet reviewed) but not ready to merge. Reviews found that agents can still choose WHICH commit the script pushes, so I built a guard: the script pushes only a develop commit that an unsandboxed step recorded (unit merge records it; Josh runs 'node scripts/unit-steps.mjs record-develop' once and after any code commit or patch he applies himself; vault/ data commits need no step). That guard needs merge to check and record the commit, which breaks about 20 existing tool tests in 4 protected files (scripts/process/unit-steps*.test.mjs, ledger-lock.test.mjs, launcher/records-writer.test.mjs) and must be redone so tests never touch the real home folder. (A, recommended, more secure) do it as part of EZD-316 or a new fix ticket: cost one more build round, about 20 test edits, one extra command for Josh after his own code commits. (B) ship without the guard: the GitHub login is locked away and every push and gh call goes through the one script, but agents still decide what lands on develop, as they do today; the guard becomes its own ticket. Which? Second item: probe 5.12 found that after a cd, a relative excluded command (node scripts/gate.mjs ...) runs a worktree copy of the script, which the sandbox can write, outside the sandbox. Is that a security hole to fix now (recommended: yes, as its own defect ticket)? Evidence: vault/plans/EZD-316.md, vault/handoff/sandbox-github.patch, worktree .claude/worktrees/EZD-316.
questions.answer: A, and fix 5.12: (A) finish the push guard in EZD-316 (the script pushes only a develop commit an unsandboxed step recorded; the ~20 tool test edits and the tests stop touching the real home folder; Josh runs record-develop after his own code commits); probe 5.12 (a relative excluded command after a cd runs a writable worktree copy outside the sandbox) gets its own defect ticket now (rule 18).

questions.question: DEFECT TICKET NEEDED (rule 17, open at front of queue; ledger entry blocked by shell hook Q-0461): Every cookie the app sets is host-only by name only. A page on any sibling of ezcontractorbinder.com can set sb-<ref>-auth-token[.N], ezd_sign_in_email or ezd_sign_in_lang with Domain=ezcontractorbinder.com, and proxy.ts:19-20, createSessionClient (supabase-server.ts:52-54) and sign-in pages (sign-in/page.tsx:24, sign-in-language.ts:7) read the first cookie of that name (@supabase/ssr 0.12.7 cookies.js:199): session fixation and sign-in email/language tampering; also the plain ezd_signed_out marker is still honoured on http. Fix: on https name every app-set cookie with the __Host- prefix via @supabase/ssr cookieOptions.name, chosen by the same x-forwarded-proto test as secure, one-time migration treating an old plain sb- cookie on https as signed out. Cost: createSessionClient is sync while jar isHttps is async, so the name is chosen before the client is built; everyone signed out once at deploy; update ARCH Auth and session. questions.question: RFC 5322 (section 3.2.3) requires a display name that contains `,` `.` `:` `;` `@` `(` `)` `[` `]` or `\` to be quoted, so a company named e.g. "Smith, Jones LLC" would be misread as two addresses, but the parent plan's T14 (d) (kept by Q-0152) expects no `"` in the From; options: (a) keep the parent's unquoted form (T10 (d) as in the parent; such names may break or show wrongly), or (b) quote the display name whenever it contains one of those characters (T10 (d) becomes `"A B cBcc: x via EZ Draft" <test@example.test>`; names without them, such as "Worth Properties via EZ Draft", are unchanged) — planner recommends (b); a technical choice, not a product one.
questions.answer: (b): a how-to-build choice; Q-0036 fixes the text "<Company> via EZ Draft", quoting is only how it is written into the header. Step 6 item 1 also removes `\` and every ASCII control character (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F) before trimming; the display name (cleaned name + SENDER_SUFFIX) is wrapped in plain double quotes, with no backslash escaping, when it contains any of `( ) [ ] : ; @ , .`, else left unquoted. T10 (d) `"A B cBcc: x via EZ Draft" <test@example.test>`; (e) `"Smith, Jones LLC via EZ Draft" <test@example.test>`; new case (f) name `O\Brien; Sons` gives `"OBrien; Sons via EZ Draft" <test@example.test>`; (a)–(c) unchanged, so "Worth Properties via EZ Draft" is sent as before. Intended change against Q-0152 (parent T14 (d) "no `"`" dropped).

questions.question: EZD-007a's security condition says the sign-in route returns one uniform response for allowed and refused emails. When `signInWithOtp` returns 429 because the same address asked again within `max_frequency` (1 s, plan D2), only a known address can hit it (the hook refuses unknown ones before any send). Does `requestSignIn` answer (a) `{ step: 'code' }` and set the cookie, as for a success (only a per-IP limit gives `too_many_requests`; T27 gains a case stubbing the per-address 429), or (b) `{ error: 'too_many_requests' }` as the plan has it now, accepting the 1-second difference as a known risk?
questions.answered_by: security-reviewer (EZD-007d, 2026-10-20); confirmed by Josh 2026-10-20 ("confirm", phase-00-for-josh.md section 2)
questions.answer: (a), narrowed: only Auth's per-IP 429 (`over_request_rate_limit`) answers `{ error: 'too_many_requests' }` with no cookie; every other 429 (including `over_email_send_rate_limit`) and the hook's 403 answer `{ step: 'code' }` and set `ezd_sign_in_email`, because both email-send limits can only be hit by a known address and (b) would reveal accounts by asking twice within 1 s. Which code the pinned Auth returns for `max_frequency` is confirmed by a new database case (two back-to-back requests: both `{ step: 'code' }`, 1 email for a member, 0 for an unknown address); T27 gains the two stubbed 429 cases.

questions.question: Chromium drops the body of a non-GET response (the app's server-action POSTs, `POST /auth/confirm` and `POST /sign-in`) when the app's own navigation commits before the read returns, and Playwright never settles the read of one aborted after its headers (vault/plans/EZD-163.md C6 iii-iv; G1, P7, P8), so no read and no safe refetch can give it; the harness leak checks (T12, T21, T23) would fail every run or at random. Options: (a) count such non-GET bodies as unread (`null`) and allow them for `fetch` and `xhr` only, while every GET, document and script body must still be read or fetched again (stricter than merged T12, which read only documents and scripts, and T21/T23, which counted unread bodies as clean); (b) route every request through the test (`context.route` + `route.fetch` + `route.fulfill`) so every body is read in Node first, at the cost of buffering every response, changing how app traffic flows under test and stacking on the net-guard route; (c) check bodies of documents and scripts only, as merged T12 did. Planner's lean: (a). It narrows a secret-leak check, so it is Josh's call (rule 16).
questions.answered_by: Josh (2026-10-27: "I want B", after asking which is more secure and robust)
questions.answer: (b), limited to the three leak-check tests (T12, T21, T23): only those specs route requests through the test (`context.route` + `route.fetch` + `route.fulfill`) so every response body, form-submit and server-action replies included, is read in Node before the page gets it; every other test and the app run unrouted. Josh chose it as the more secure and robust option (CLAUDE.md rule 18): no unread body, no blind spot where secrets are most likely. EZD-163 set to todo for the planner to re-plan with this answer.

questions.question: Throttle details: what counts toward the per-IP limit, whether refused attempts count, whether a success clears earlier failures, rolling windows, IPv6 /64, loopback and missing addresses, and the HMAC key derivation.
questions.answer: (i) changed: toward the per-IP 30, every sign-in email request and every wrong password, code or bad link counts; successful checks, Supabase 429 and 5xx do not. (ii) refused attempts are not counted. (iii) a success does not clear earlier failures (the earlier "success clears the count" sentence is withdrawn; it was not in Q-0094). (iv) rolling windows. (v) IPv6 by /64, IPv4 by full address. (vi) changed: no IP counting only when VERCEL_ENV is unset (local, CI); on Vercel, loopback, private, carrier-NAT, link-local, unparseable or missing addresses count as "unknown"; read only the client-IP header Vercel guarantees to overwrite (confirm on pinned platform). (vii) the throttle key is derived with HKDF from SUPABASE_API_GATE_SECRET under its own label; never sent to the database, logged or stored. Josh can override.
questions.source: Q-0094; R26 R14; RFC 5869 §3.1; 02 Stack; vault/plans/EZD-033.md

questions.question: When Auth refuses a password sign-in for its captcha (no password was checked), does the attempt count toward the password throttle? Q-0104 (i) counts every wrong password and does not count Supabase 429 and 5xx, and does not name this case. Options: (a) do not count it, like 429 and 5xx (recommended by the planner: the password was never checked, and counting it would let a script without a captcha token use up a person's password attempts); (b) count it, as `signInWithPassword` counts every other refusal today.
questions.answer: (a): a captcha refusal does not count toward the password throttle (per-email or per-IP), like a Supabase 429 or 5xx: Auth checks the captcha before the credentials, so no password was checked, and counting it would let a script with no token lock a person out of password sign-in for 15 minutes. As merged, actions.ts counts it (only 429 and status 0/5xx settle), so EZD-034 adds a settle branch matched on Auth's captcha error code, never on bare HTTP 400 (a wrong password is also 400 and stays counted).

questions.answer: Adopt the proposed rule: a failed outbox write or failed post-save record update keeps the change(s) in an in-memory pending list in order (plus later enqueues while the failure stands); retry() writes/commits the list first, then clears problem and drains; status never becomes saved while the list is non-empty. questions.question: 11 Budgets gives download budgets as "compressed JavaScript" in "KB" but no source says which compression or how many bytes a KB is, and the tests compare exact byte counts. questions.question: Realtime checks access only when a channel is joined, so after a user is deactivated or loses a project from their list, a tab they already have open keeps receiving that project's live lock, presence, job-progress and review-count messages until their access token expires (the Supabase default lifetime, which no vault source states; 11 Operations says such changes "end their sessions"); the options are (a) accept that window and document it, since the messages carry ids and counters only; (b) shorten the access-token lifetime for everyone (for example to 10 minutes), which costs one token request per open tab per lifetime and more Auth refreshes; or (c) (a) plus a server push on the user's own channel, sent by the trigger that ends their sessions, that makes the app drop its project channels and rejoin at once (the rejoin is refused), with the token lifetime as the hard limit for a tampered browser.
questions.answer: (c): keep the payload rule; the database pushes `session.ended` on the user's own channel whenever their sessions are ended (the app drops all channels and goes to sign-in); access-token lifetime pinned explicitly at 3600 s as the hard limit for a tampered browser; `current_app_user_id()` returns null for an ended session so routes fail closed at 401. Josh can override.
questions.source: 11 Operations; 03 rules 1 and 2; R26 R2; vault/plans/EZD-006.md Step 3; vault/plans/EZD-018.md Step 3

# EZD-291 · Fix: the EZD-102 D5 permissions realtime test does not depend on fixed waits

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-291-1, AC-EZD-291-2
- **Complexity:** medium
- **Areas:** testing, realtime
- **User-visible result:** none in the app; the live permission-change test stops failing at random.
- Phase: 1 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-02 · Status: questions

## 1. What to build
Row: phase-01.md:164. Every file is a test or harness file (`.claude/hooks/guard-paths.mjs` `isTest`, lines 29–31).

**Cause** (P1–P4, R-048): local Realtime stops its broadcast stream 10 minutes after it starts (`{:shutdown, :rebalancing}`, tenant region `us-east-1` vs unset node region); its slot is temporary, so `realtime.send` rows written before the next channel join are never delivered, while the joined D5 channel stays `SUBSCRIBED`. A step straddling that moment gets 0 events whatever the wait. **Fix:** a probe broadcast proves the stream live before each step (a join restarts it when the probe is lost); a second probe after the step is the fence (delivery is in commit order); a step repeats once only when the stream provably broke inside it. D5 keeps no fixed sleep.

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `app/test-harness/realtime/stream.ts` | new | section 3 rows | `app/test-harness/permissions/load-plan.ts` (header comment, `../rls/db` types) | `pnpm run typecheck` |
| 2 | `app/test-harness/realtime/stream.test.ts` | new | none; J1–J8 | `app/test-harness/permissions/load-plan.test.ts` | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec vitest run test-harness/realtime/stream.test.ts` |
| 3 | `app/src/server/permissions/permissions.db.test.ts` | change: lines 1–8 header comment, imports (lines 23–31), D5 (lines 124–173); add D5c after D5 | none | its own D5 | V1 |

V1 (AC-1, file alone; after `pnpm db:up`): `cd app && for i in $(seq 1 20); do pnpm exec vitest run src/server/permissions/permissions.db.test.ts || exit 1; done`. V2 (AC-1, full suite): 20 runs of `cd app && pnpm exec vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/ezd291-$i.json`; in each JSON the assertions whose `fullName` contains `D5 broadcast` and `D5c control` have `status` `passed`, checked with `node -e` (EZD-285 V2). V3 (the found cause): loop the file alone for at least 12 minutes, then `docker logs --since 15m supabase_realtime_ezdraft 2>&1 | grep rebalancing` shows at least one line inside the loop's window and every run passed; report the line's time and the run count. Another test's failure is reported by name (rule 16). Then `node scripts/gate.mjs <worktree>`.

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who | Test-author writes rows 1–3, runs V1–V3 and the gate, reports the counts | guard-paths.mjs; EZD-285 section 8 |
| Probe | `sendProbe`: `nonce = randomUUID()` (`node:crypto`); `` await sql`select private.broadcast_user(${appUserId}::uuid, 'test.probe', jsonb_build_object('probe', ${nonce}::text))` ``; returns `nonce`. Received payload is `{ probe: nonce }` (`toEventPayload` drops `id`) | P6; ARCH Realtime "Payload rule"; lesson EZD-018 (jsonb built in SQL, not a bound string) |
| Stream pid | `streamPid`: run `STREAM_PID_SQL`; first row's `active_pid` as `Number`, `null` when no row | P2; `scripts/db/realtime-warmup.mjs` `SLOT_ACTIVE_SQL` (same slot prefix) |
| `waitForStream(sql)` | poll `streamPid` every 250 ms until non-null or `JOIN_WAIT_MS` passed; returns the last value | `realtime-warmup.mjs` `waitForBroadcastStream` (250 ms interval) |
| `ensureStream` | Try 1: `sendProbe`; `await waitFor(() => probeIndex(channel.events, nonce) >= 0, JOIN_WAIT_MS)`; seen → return `{ nonce, pid: await streamPid(sql) }`. Not seen → restart the stream: `const k = await connectRealtime(accessToken); await k.join(channel.topic).joined; await waitForStream(sql)` (k stays open; `closeAllRealtime` in afterAll closes it). Try 2: same probe and wait; not seen → `throw new Error('realtime_stream_unavailable')` | P1 (a join restarts the stream); R-048 Q3 |
| `fencedStep` | For `attempt` 1 and 2: `await restore?.()`; `start = await ensureStream(…)`; `statusesBefore = channel.statuses.length`; `await run()` (a throw propagates, no retry); `end = await sendProbe(sql, appUserId)`; `fenceSeen = await waitFor(() => probeIndex(channel.events, end) >= 0, JOIN_WAIT_MS)`; `pidAfter = await streamPid(sql)`; `stepOutcome({ fenceSeen, pidBefore: start.pid, pidAfter, statusesBefore, statusesAfter: channel.statuses.length })` = `'complete'` → return `{ arrived: eventsBetween(channel.events, start.nonce, end, event) ?? [], attempts: attempt }`. After attempt 2 → `throw new Error('realtime_stream_interrupted')` | P1, P4; ticket row ("received or a bounded timeout") |
| `stepOutcome` | `'complete'` only when `fenceSeen` and `pidBefore !== null` and `pidBefore === pidAfter` and `statusesAfter === statusesBefore`; else `'interrupted'` | P1 (a restart gives a new slot and walsender); node-client `statuses` (a rejoin adds statuses) |
| `probeIndex` | first index whose `event === PROBE_EVENT` and whose `payload` is a non-null object with `probe === nonce`; `-1` when none | — |
| `eventsBetween` | `s = probeIndex(events, startNonce)`, `e = probeIndex(events, endNonce)`; `null` when `s < 0`, `e < 0` or `e < s`; else `events.slice(s + 1, e).filter((x) => x.event === name)` | — |
| Why a repeat is not a weaker check | It happens only when the stream broke (fence missing, walsender changed, channel rejoined); a lost app event on a live stream returns `arrived` `[]` and D5 fails (D5c) | ticket row; CLAUDE.md rule 16 |
| Step order and bodies in D5 | (a) `run`: line 138–139 update. (b) `run`: line 144–147 update, `expect(r.count).toBe(37)` kept. (c) `restore`: `` insert into public.user_permission (tenant_id, membership_id, permission_key, granted) values (${tenant}::uuid, ${m.membershipId}::uuid, 'edit_model', true) on conflict (membership_id, permission_key) do nothing ``; `run`: line 153–154 delete. (d) `restore`: the line 153–154 delete; `run`: line 159–160 insert. Restores run before the start probe, so their events are never counted | EZD-102 D5 row; migration `20261024100005_create_user_permission.sql` line 8 (primary key) |
| D5 per step | `const { arrived } = await fencedStep({ sql, channel: own, appUserId: m.appUserId, accessToken: s.accessToken, event: EVENT, restore, run })`; `expect(arrived, name).toHaveLength(1)`; `expect(arrived[0].payload, name).toEqual({})`. Keep `expect(await own.joined).toBe('SUBSCRIBED')` and the 90,000 ms limit. Remove the `sleep(QUIET_MS)` lines and the `QUIET_MS`, `sleep`, `waitFor`, `eventsNamed`, `JOIN_WAIT_MS` imports D5 no longer uses | EZD-102 D5 row; ticket row |
| D5c control | Title `D5c control: a delete whose event is never sent fails the D5 check (EZD-291)`; new member with `['view_projects']`, own sign-in and channel, `joined` `SUBSCRIBED`; `fencedStep` with the (c) `restore` and `run: () => sql.begin(async (tx) => { await tx\`set local session_replication_role = replica\`; await <(c) delete on tx> })`; `expect(arrived).toEqual([])`; `expect(() => expect(arrived, '(c) delete one row').toHaveLength(1)).toThrow()`. No assertion on `attempts` (a rebalance may land in it). Limit 60,000 ms | P5 (replica role skips the trigger, transaction-local) |
| Header comment | lines 1–8 now cite EZD-291 for D5 and D5c and name `stream.ts` instead of the two wait constants | lesson EZD-152 (comments restate the new rule) |

### Do not touch
`app/test-harness/realtime/node-client.ts`; D1–D3; the migrations; `scripts/` (build-system freeze); `supabase/config.toml`.

Ticket row: phase-01.md:164 (Scope, Done when, Depends on EZD-102 and EZD-285, Spec ref Q-0268, rule 17).

## 2. Sources
- Q-0476 (QUESTIONS.md): the failure; Q-0268 and CLAUDE.md rules 16–17. EZD-102 plan section 4 row D5 (what D5 checks: exactly 1 `user_permission.updated` `{}` per statement for steps (a)–(d)).
- ARCH Realtime (EZD-018): private user topic, `private.broadcast_user`, payload `id` dropped by `toEventPayload`.
- Probes on the local stack, develop `0a1bbce6`, 2026-11-02:
  - P1: realtime v2.143.4 log: `18:09:08 Starting replication for Broadcast Changes`, `18:19:08 Tenant realtime-dev has been terminated: {:shutdown, :rebalancing}`, `Disconnecting broadcast changes handler in the step : :streaming`; `pg_replication_slots` then empty until the next join (`18:38:40 Starting replication`).
  - P2: `pg_replication_slots`: `supabase_realtime_messages_replication_slot_ | temporary t | active t | active_pid 1747`.
  - P3: `_realtime.extensions` region `us-east-1`; the container sets no `REGION` (only `SEED_SELF_HOST=true`).
  - P4: untimed loop of 45 D5 runs: 45 passed (the 18:48:40 stop fell between runs; the next run's join restarted it at 18:48:45). One run started 8 s before the next stop (18:58:45): step (d) failed `expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0` at line 170 (Q-0476's message); stream back at 18:58:58.
  - P5 (rolled back): with `set local session_replication_role = replica` a `user_permission` delete wrote 0 `user_permission.updated` rows to `realtime.messages`; with `origin`, 1.
  - P6 (rolled back): `private.broadcast_user(…, 'test.probe', jsonb_build_object('probe','x'))` as the harness role wrote 1 row, payload `{"id": …, "probe": "x"}`.
- R-048: rebalance check `REBALANCE_CHECK_INTERVAL_IN_MS` default 600,000 ms, stops on a region mismatch whatever clients are joined; slot `TEMPORARY`; joined channels are not closed; the stream restarts only at the next channel join; `config.toml` `[realtime]` cannot set the interval.
- Code: `node-client.ts` (`connectRealtime`, `TestChannel`, `ReceivedEvent`, `waitFor`, `JOIN_WAIT_MS` 10,000); `rls/db.ts` (`Sql`); `rls/fixtures.ts` (`harnessSql`, `signIn`).
- S15 Entry points and decisions 04, 10 (tickets.json) govern nothing here (Spec ref: Q-0268, rule 17).

Architecture: Realtime (EZD-018); Tests

Risks: other Realtime event tests share the cause (Q-0479); hosted exposure unverified (Q-0480). D5 gets faster (no 3,000 ms sleeps).

- **Q-0479:** answered-agent (a): a separate defect ticket moves the other event tests onto `stream.ts` after this ticket; this ticket stays D5-only. No plan change.

# EZD-110b · Notifications: bell and list

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-110-1, AC-EZD-110-2, AC-EZD-110-3, AC-EZD-110-4, AC-EZD-110-7
- **Complexity:** medium (section 8)
- **Areas:** ui, tokens, testing
- **User-visible result:** on `/dev/notifications` Josh sends himself a test notification; the bell's amber dot appears without a reload; the list shows it (icon, title, project, time); clicking it opens `/` and marks it read; Mark all read clears the dot and Show older loads the next 20.
- Phase: 2 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-10-30 · Re-validated 2026-11-03 against EZD-318; Q-0549 (b) applied; D15, B2, T14 redesigned 2026-11-04 for Q-0550 (one version rule) · Status: ready

Source: `vault/plans/EZD-110.md` Split proposal row EZD-110b. D-n rows come from that plan (D15 redesigned, Q-0550); D1–D12, D14, D26, D28 and the SQL, route, server and job contracts are EZD-110a's, cited by number only. B-n rows are this part's.

## 1. What to build

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D13 Events | `notification.created` (insert trigger) and `notification.read` (open, mark all); the store refetches on every event, so counts never come from a payload | 11 rule 11; ARCH Realtime payload rule |
| D15 Store | **Version rule (the one stale-page guard):** a private integer `version` goes up by one at exactly three points: a first page applying, every `reset()` call, every `applyRead()` call (also when nothing changes; ok `markAllRead`/`open` change state only through it). A fetch records `version` when it starts; if it moved by the time the fetch settles, the fetch changes nothing on success or failure (every field and flag stays): a stale first page only sets `wanted`, so the run's loop fetches once more (no inner retry); a stale older fetch is dropped. A bump while `olderStatus` is `'loading'` sets it `'idle'` in the same change (Show older shows again). **Run:** `refresh()` sets a private `wanted` flag, starts the run if none is running and returns the running run's promise. The run loops while `wanted`: clear it, record `version`, fetch the first page, apply per the rule; it clears its running handle in the same synchronous step as its last `wanted` check (not in `.finally`). Many `refresh()` calls during a fetch cost one more fetch. **A first page applies:** it MERGES only when no replace is pending, an older page is loaded, `page.hasMore` is true and the page's last id is among the loaded items: `items` = the page's items, then the loaded items after that id (in order, ids in the page skipped), `unreadCount` = the page's, `hasMore` unchanged, `olderStatus` per the bump rule. Every other first page REPLACES: `items`, `hasMore`, `unreadCount` = the page's, `olderStatus` `'idle'`, older pages forgotten, pending replace cleared (a `hasMore` false page is the whole list; one not reaching the loaded items would leave a gap). **`reset()`** (resync) bumps, keeps the shown state in every `status` (items, count, dot; Q-0549 (b)), marks a replace pending until a first page applies, then `refresh()`. **`loadOlder()`**: cursor = last item; no bump; success appends unseen ids, sets `hasMore`, `unreadCount` = the page's, `olderStatus` `'idle'`, older page loaded. `applyRead(id)`: a loaded item with that id and `readAt` null gets `readAt` = `new Date().toISOString()` and `unreadCount` − 1 (not below 0); not loaded or already read → no state change (D16's following `refresh()` brings the server count). `applyRead(null)`: every loaded item with `readAt` null gets it set the same way; `unreadCount` 0 (null is sent only by mark-all, M3). `open(id)`: ok → exactly `applyRead(id)`, return the result; not ok → `await refresh()`, then return the result (D17's toast follows the refetch); `api.open` rejecting counts as `{ ok: false, messageKey: 'error.db_unavailable' }`. `markAllRead()`: ok → exactly `applyRead(null)`, `true`; failure → state unchanged, `false`. No method rejects (failed fetches set `status`/`olderStatus` `'error'`) | `permission-store.ts` pattern; M3 (`unreadCount` counts every unread row, loaded or not); D24 (dot and label follow `unreadCount`); review-phase-02 item 4; Q-0549; Q-0550 |
| D16 Bell wiring | Store created once per mount with `notificationHttpApi`; the effect is `useEffect(() => connectNotificationBell(store, getRealtimeHub().user()), [store])`. `connectNotificationBell(store, h)` (section 3): `refresh()`; `h.on('notification.created')` → `refresh()`, `h.on('notification.read')` → `applyRead(p.notificationId)` then `refresh()`, `h.onResync` → `reset()`; it reads no `h.ready` and calls no `h.onStatus`; returns the cleanup: the three offs, then `h.release()`. The hub resyncs every handle on every SUBSCRIBED, the first join included (EZD-318 D1, D5), covering the gap before it. Refused (EZD-318 D6, D7): the list stays as fetched on mount; a later subscribe's resync runs `reset()` once. Mount cost: exactly two `GET /api/notifications` when the user channel subscribes (mount `refresh()`, first resync's `reset()`; D15 runs them as one run when they overlap), one when refused. Opening the panel calls `refresh()` when `status` is `idle` or `error`. No timers | `PermissionsProvider.tsx`; `hub.ts`; EZD-318 D1, D5–D7; ARCH Realtime Resync; AC-EZD-110-1; ARCH Realtime no-polling lint |
| D17 Click item | `store.open(id)`; ok → close panel, `router.push(link)` (`useRouter`, `next/navigation`); not ok → `useToast().show({ message: messageKey })`, panel stays open | AC-3, AC-7; Q-0058 |
| D18 Mark all read | Shown only when `unreadCount > 0`; failure → toast `error.db_unavailable` | board 01c (shown with unread, absent when empty) |
| D19 Show older | Shown when `hasMore`; a failed older load replaces it with `InlineError` `office.notifications.load_failed` + Retry (`loadOlder`) | Q-0425; ARCH State components |
| D20 Panel states | `idle`/`loading` with no items: `SkeletonGroup` of 3 `Skeleton` 56 px rows; `error`: `InlineError` `office.notifications.load_failed` + Retry (`refresh`), whether or not items are loaded (S01 States; B2 keeps the items, shown again on Retry's success); `ready` + no items: empty body (`notifications_off` 28 px `--ez-slate-300`, text) and no Mark all read or Show older | board 01c; ARCH State components |
| D21 Times | Local time zone (Intl default). `now - created < 60 s` (or negative) → `just_now`; `< 60 min` → `minutes_ago {count}`; same calendar day → `hours_ago {count}` (floor); previous calendar day → `yesterday {time}`; same year → `date {date}`; else `date_year {date, year}`. `time` = `hour:'numeric', minute:'2-digit'`, `date` = `month:'short', day:'numeric'`, with U+202F and U+00A0 replaced by U+0020. Computed at render; no timer | board 01c; Q-0058 timers rule |

| D25 Dev page | `notFound()` in production. Values only: `MessagesProvider` (office, en) and `StateHost`; a `HeaderCard` holding a flex spacer, `NotificationBell`, then two empty spans 42 px and 32 px wide (gap 16) so the bell sits where board 01c puts it; below, `NotificationsProbe`: one button per kind whose text is the kind code, posting `{ kind, projectId?, params: DEV_SAMPLE_PARAMS[kind] }`; `DEV_SAMPLE_PARAMS` and `?project=<uuid>` as EZD-110a built them | Q-0413; EZD-024 dev page (values only) |
| D27 Language | Office surface and all notification emails English | Q-0121 (a) |
| B1 Panel container | `Popover.Content` sits inside `Popover.Portal` (HeaderCard has `overflow: hidden`, which would clip it); `Popover.Root` is controlled (`open` in `useState(false)`, `onOpenChange`) so D17 can close it; `data-testid="notification-panel"` is on `Popover.Content`, which wraps `NotificationPanelView` | `app/src/components/shell/HeaderCard.module.css`; D17 |
| B2 Store state | State objects are immutable: every change builds a new `NotificationState` and notifies subscribers once; `get()` returns the same object until the next change (`useSyncExternalStore(store.subscribe, store.get, store.get)`); a bump that changes no field notifies nobody. Each first-page fetch sets `status` `'loading'` at its start only from `'idle'` or `'error'`; a page applying → `'ready'`; a failure with `version` unmoved → `'error'` with `items`, `unreadCount`, `hasMore` unchanged and a pending replace kept; with `wanted` set the next fetch starts at once (`'loading'` again). `loadOlder()` resolves at once with no fetch when `hasMore` is false, `items` is empty, or `olderStatus` is `'loading'`; otherwise `olderStatus` `'loading'`; success per D15; failure with `version` unmoved → `'error'`, items unchanged. | D15; `permission-store.ts`; Q-0550 |

Every call `cache: 'no-store'` | route error body `{ error: { code, message_key } }` in `app/src/app/api/settings/customers/[id]/route.ts:27`; D10 |

## 3. Interface contract

| Kind | Name or path | Details |

## 6. Proposed wording
Board text is used as drawn (S01c: "Notifications", "Mark all read", "Show older", "No notifications yet", "Notifications, N new", "Unread"/"Read", "{n} min ago", "Yesterday 4:12 PM", "Oct 26"). Not on a board, added by this part:

## 7. Security review
security-review: no. This part adds no table, policy, route, migration or permission read; the stored link it navigates to is checked by EZD-110a's `link` constraint (D2) and the open route's guard (D8, D10), which EZD-110a's security review covers.
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer always · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier yes · security-reviewer no.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
Medium: browser-only logic (a single-flight store, a time formatter, a Radix popover) on contracts EZD-110a already proved, across 10 build rows and 8 tests. Test-author and builder `claude-sonnet-5-5`.

## 9. Dependencies
- Row: EZD-110a (table, routes, events, `kinds.ts`, dev page and probe), EZD-015 (= EZD-015a, b, c; states, toasts, done), EZD-016a (browser harness, done; visual checklist).

- Risk: EZD-108 and this ticket both edit `EXPECTED_ICONS`; whichever merges second takes develop's list (section 4). Steps 7, 17, 21 and 22 edit files EZD-110a creates, so this part builds only after EZD-110a merges.

None. QP-1 answered by Q-0549 (b); Q-0550 (one version rule, T14 matrix) applied in D15, B2 and T14.
