# EZD-331 · Fix: the dead-lock take-over tests pass while other lanes run their gates

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-331-1, AC-EZD-331-2
- **Complexity:** low
- **Areas:** tooling, scripts
- **User-visible result:** the gate no longer fails at random on the EZD-256 lock tests when several lanes run gates at once, and a gate step that dies without output now says why.
- Phase: 1 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-04 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build

Cause (evidence in section 2, E1-E6). "Not a git repository" is not the failure: it is the first stdout line of every fixture gate (`printTouched` on a temp folder that is no git repository, `scripts/gate.mjs` lines 89-90), quoted at the head of K12's assertion message. The failure was K12 round 0 line 353: the lane 2 fixture gate's `test` step (`npm run test`) failed with zero output, not even npm's `> ezd256-fixture@0.0.0 test` banner, inside a 1.34 s round (E1). So the machine's `npm` process ended before it wrote anything, and `run()` in `scripts/gate.mjs` (lines 289-310) drops `r.error` and `r.signal`, so the reason was lost (E2). Shared lock paths, shared temp paths, process kills, a kernel process limit and the file's own concurrency are ruled out (E3-E6); the failure did not reproduce. Fix for the cause the evidence points to: (a) the fixture gates in `gate-lock.test.mjs` run their checks through a fixture-local `npm` that starts no machine npm, takes no PATH lookup of `node` and reads no `~/.npm`; (b) the gate names a spawn error or a signal of any step, so a recurrence carries its cause. No lock code and no existing assertion changes (AC-EZD-331-2).

### Build steps

(a) new const `FAKE_NPM(fixtureDir: string): string` returning the exact text of Decided "fixture npm"; (b) `mkFixture()` also writes `<fixture>/hold.cjs` with the text of the existing `HOLD` const, writes `<fixture>/bin/npm` with `FAKE_NPM(fixture)` then `chmodSync(<fixture>/bin/npm, 0o755)`, and sets package.json `scripts.test` to `node hold.cjs` (typecheck, lint, build stay `node -e "process.exit(0)"`); (c) `envFor(extra)` adds `NPM_CALLS: path.join(tmp, 'npm-calls.txt')` always, and `PATH: \`${path.join(fixture, 'bin')}${path.delimiter}${process.env.PATH}\`` when `fixture` is set, both before `...extra`; (d) new tests K18 and K19 (section 4) inside the existing `describe('EZD-256 dead lock take-over')`, after K17 and before K14. K1-K17 bodies and assertions unchanged | `scripts/launcher/ci-gate.test.mjs` lines 23-34 (shim folder on PATH, `chmodSync 0o755`) | `node --test scripts/process/gate-lock.test.mjs` prints `# pass 19` and `# fail 0` |

In `run()` only, replace `const out = \`${r.stdout \|\| ''}${r.stderr \|\| ''}\`;` with: `const text = \`${r.stdout \|\| ''}${r.stderr \|\| ''}\`;` `const why = [...(r.error ? Nothing else in the file changes | `laneFailure` in the same file, line 246 (`r.error.message`, `signal ${r.signal}`) | `node --test scripts/ci/__tests__/gate-failures.test.mjs scripts/process/gate-summary.test.mjs scripts/process/gate-lock.test.mjs` all pass; then `node scripts/gate.mjs <EZD-331 worktree>` |

### Decided for the builder

### Do not touch
`scripts/gate-lock.mjs`; every line of `scripts/gate.mjs` outside `run()`; K1-K17 in `gate-lock.test.mjs` (bodies, loop counts, timeouts, messages); G1-G3; `scripts/gate-summary.mjs`.

Ticket row (phase-01.md): Scope: Q-0580 (rule 17 defect; Josh 2026-11-04, chat: "Yes, file it"): during EZD-117b's gate, while lanes 2 and 3 ran gates at the same time, two EZD-256 tests in `scripts/process/gate-lock.test.mjs` ("K12 two lane gates, one dead sweep lock, loop" and the "dead lock take-over" group) failed with "Not a git repository"; run alone the file passes 17 of 17. Find the cause and make these tests safe beside concurrent lane gates without weakening what they check. Guarded files follow PROCESS.md rule 19 (interactive fix mode). / Done when: `scripts/process/gate-lock.test.mjs` passes on every run of a loop of 10 runs while two other lane gates run at the same time (test). Each K12 and dead-lock take-over test still fails when the take-over is not atomic (test). / Depends on: EZD-256 / Spec ref: Q-0580, rule 17.

## 2. Sources
- Q-0580 (`vault/questions/QUESTIONS-answered.md`): file the defect, fix mode. `vault/handoff/build-watch-2026-11-04.md` line 28.
- E1: `.claude/worktrees/EZD-117b/gate.log` lines 5973-6026 (2026-11-04 23:18Z gate): K12 round 0 failed at line 353 (`k.status` 1, expected 0) for the lane 2 gate, whose console shows typecheck, lint and build banners but an empty `test` step; `lane sweep: lane 1 skipped (sweep pid 627)` passed line 349; round duration 1341 ms. `gate-failures.log` line 4 shows the TOUCHED PATHS line as the error.
- E2: `scripts/gate.mjs` 289-310: `out` is stdout plus stderr only; `scripts/gate-summary.mjs` line 39 prints the last 8 non-empty lines, here none, so no line of npm ran. Node's `spawnSync` gives `r.error.message` `spawnSync <cmd> ENOENT` and `r.signal` `SIGKILL` for a killed child (both run in this session).
- E3: every fixture gate gets its own `TMPDIR` (gate-lock.test.mjs 78-86), so lock, sweep, lease and stage paths (gate.mjs 116, 165, 217-219) never meet a real gate's.
- E4: no code under `scripts/` signals another process (grep of `process.kill(`, `.kill(`, pkill, lsof in this session: only `kill(pid, 0)` probes and own-child kills).

## 5. Visual checklist
None (no screen changes).

## 6. Proposed wording
None (pure functions; refusal messages belong to the Move and Wall tools, EZD-210, EZD-212).

## 7. Security review
security-review: yes. Areas: API and data model (the save route's validation now requires wall `layers` and migrates v1 objects to v2 before storing; EZD-202 Save check).
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer always · calc-auditor yes (lengths, faces, areas, joins) · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer yes.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
High: a schema version change that reaches the save route and other tickets' tests, plus geometry with tolerance edge cases. Test-author Opus 5.5 (calculation-heavy, PROCESS.md section 4); builder Opus 5.5 / medium.

## 9. Dependencies
- EZD-202 (row): schema modules, `tolerance.ts`, `migrate.ts`, samples, save check.
- Missing from the row: EZD-201 (`MAX_WALL_LENGTH_IN` in `src/length.ts`, imported by step 7; review-phase-04 items 2, 7). EZD-238 (step E4 edits its test file; phase 3, merged before phase 4 builds; review-phase-04 item 7). EZD-120a (E3's save route) and EZD-120b (E6's `loadModel` test), both done.
- Not needed: EZD-016a (no screen).
- EZD-205 (dependent): its closure chains use corners only ("walls joined end to end by corners", EZD-205 plan), so the new `cross` kind leaves them unchanged; its outlines line "P203 Decided Joins leaves crossings to EZD-205" is now stale (crossings are reported as `cross`, Q-0598), for the orchestrator.
- Risks: EZD-236 (depends on EZD-202 only) generates walls and should depend on EZD-203 (missing dependency, for the orchestrator). Code or tests building wall data without `layers` fail typecheck or validation (E5, step 11). Performance: `moveWall` is linear in one level's walls, far under the 50 ms commit budget at 3,000 objects (11 Budgets).

## 10. Open questions
- **Q-0583 (answered-agent, phase-auditor; 09e line 7, Q-0570):** (a) a move that would pull a wall's end off the wall it meets (a T join, or a rotated stretched wall a partition's end falls off) is refused with `join_lost`. Built in Decided Move algorithm step 8; tests T17, T18.
- **Q-0598 (answered-agent, phase-auditor; Q-0570, 00e Join, Q-0583 (a)):** a crossing is a join (`cross`); a move must keep it, else `join_lost`. Built in Decided Joins, Join order, Move algorithm steps 5 and 8; section 3 `WallJoin`; tests T10, T24.

# EZD-206 · Snapping

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-206-1, AC-EZD-206-2
- **Complexity:** medium (section 8)
- **Areas:** geometry, testing, performance
- **User-visible result:** none on screen yet; the snap rules (endpoints, midpoints, wall faces, 90/45°, 1/2" increment) and the lookup that finds nearby walls exist as tested functions that the canvas hover (EZD-207) and the Wall tool's snap marker (EZD-210) use.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-04 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build
Three modules in `@ezdraft/geometry` under `packages/geometry/src/snap/`: a uniform-grid spatial index (generic ids and rectangles), a wall snap index on top of it, and `snap()`. No UI, no data, no dependency. Units: model inches, +x east, +y north (EZD-203 Decided Axes).

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `packages/geometry/src/snap/spatial-index.test.ts` (test-author) | new | none; tests S1–S5 (section 4) | `packages/geometry/src/index.test.ts` (describe + vitest imports) | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry test` fails (red) |
| 2 | `packages/geometry/src/snap/snap.test.ts` (test-author) | new | none; tests N1–N20 (section 4); imports `wallObj`, `ID` from `../walls/test-utils/fixtures` (EZD-203 step 1) | `packages/geometry/src/index.test.ts` | same, red |
| 3 | `packages/geometry/src/snap/spatial-index.ts` | new | `type Rect = { minX: number; minY: number; maxX: number; maxY: number }`; `const SPATIAL_INDEX_CELL_IN = 48`; `interface SpatialIndex { upsert(id: string, bounds: Rect): void; remove(id: string): boolean; query(rect: Rect): string[]; size(): number; lastQueryExamined(): number }`; `function createSpatialIndex(cellSizeIn?: number): SpatialIndex` | `packages/geometry/src/walls/wall.ts` (EZD-203: plain exported functions and types, no classes) | S1–S5 green |
| 4 | `packages/geometry/src/snap/wall-snap-index.ts` | new | `interface WallSnapIndex { readonly spatial: SpatialIndex; upsertWall(wall: WallObject): void; removeWall(id: string): boolean; getWall(id: string): WallObject \| undefined }`; `function createWallSnapIndex(walls: readonly WallObject[]): WallSnapIndex`; `function wallBounds(data: WallData): Rect` | step 3 file | S5, N19, N20 green |
| 5 | `packages/geometry/src/snap/snap.ts` | new | `const SNAP_KINDS = ['endpoint', 'midpoint', 'face', 'angle', 'increment'] as const`; `type SnapKind = (typeof SNAP_KINDS)[number]`; `const SNAP_CAPTURE_PX = 10`; `const SNAP_CAPTURE_DEG = 5`; `const DEFAULT_SNAP_INCREMENT_IN = 0.5`; `type SnapSettings = { endpoints: boolean; midpoints: boolean; faces: boolean; angles: boolean; increment: boolean; incrementIn: number }`; `const DEFAULT_SNAP_SETTINGS: Readonly<SnapSettings>` (frozen; all five `true`, `incrementIn: 0.5`); `type SnapRequest = { cursor: Point; pixelsPerInch: number; anchor: Point \| null; referenceDirection: Point \| null; excludeIds?: readonly string[]; settings?: SnapSettings }`; `type SnapResult = { point: Point; kind: SnapKind \| null; wallId: string \| null }`; `function snap(index: WallSnapIndex, request: SnapRequest): SnapResult` | `packages/geometry/src/walls/move.ts` (EZD-203: result object, never throws) | N1–N18 green |
| 6 | `packages/geometry/src/snap/index.ts` | new | `export * from './spatial-index'; export * from './wall-snap-index'; export * from './snap';` | `packages/geometry/src/walls/index.ts` (EZD-203 step 10) | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry typecheck` |
| 7 | `packages/geometry/src/index.ts` | change | add one line `export * from './snap/index';` | existing lines of that file | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry test` all green; `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry lint` |

Functions this plan calls and does not create (L-043): `wallFaceLines(data: WallData): { left: WallLine; right: WallLine }`, types `WallObject`, `WallLine` (`packages/geometry/src/walls/wall.ts`, EZD-203 s3); `pointsEqual(p: Point, q: Point): boolean` (`packages/geometry/src/tolerance.ts`, EZD-202 s3); `wallObj(id: string, start: Point, end: Point, opts?: { level?: string; thicknessSide?: 'left' \| 'right' \| 'center' }): WallObject`, `ID` (`packages/geometry/src/walls/test-utils/fixtures.ts`, EZD-203 step 1); types `Point` (`schema/common.ts`), `WallData` (`schema/wall.ts`) (EZD-202 s3). All present on develop at 0f726433 (EZD-203 merged; re-validated 2026-11-05).

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |

# EZD-236 · Benchmark project generator

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-236-1, AC-EZD-236-2, AC-EZD-236-3
- **Complexity:** high (section 8)
- **Areas:** data-model, migrations, security, testing
- **User-visible result:** none on screen yet: an owner's request makes the company's 3,000-object benchmark project, which opens in the editor and never shows on Projects (EZD-207, EZD-237 build on it).
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-05 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build

## 7. Security review
security-review: yes. Areas: migrations (M1–M3), permissions (two keys, route and SQL), data access (definer RPC writing through `save_objects`, tenant from the claim), API (new production route).
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer always · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer yes.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
high: a definer function that nests another definer's checks, a guard that relies on `current_user` semantics, and a redefinition of another ticket's functions, all unprobed on the pinned stack (L-009). Test-author Sonnet 5.5 / medium; builder Opus 5.5 / medium (PROCESS.md section 4).

## 9. Dependencies
- Row: EZD-202 (schema, `parseModelDocument`, level check), EZD-017 (done), EZD-120a (`model_object`, `save_objects`, first-floor trigger), EZD-120b (model route), EZD-120c (editor route, `__ezdraftEditor`), EZD-120d (part of EZD-120).
- Missing from the row: **EZD-203** (wall `layers`, `createWallData`, `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` 2; P203 s3, s9), **EZD-205a** (room `status`, `closureOverride`, version 3, inside-face outlines; P205 part a), **EZD-117b** (M2 redefines its `list_projects`/`count_projects`; slice 2 precedes slice 4, PHASES.md), EZD-102 and EZD-133 (done: `requireApiPermission`, money scan), EZD-016a (done: browser harness for B1).
- Risks: (a) later project lists (EZD-127, EZD-128) must add `not is_benchmark` (step 9 rule). (b) A schema change fails G2, so that ticket updates the generator. (c) `edit_model` users can edit the benchmark and drift later runs (EZD-237's). (d) 3,000 changes is the largest save yet; hosted request size unmeasured. (e) No P205a plan exists yet (split proposal only): when it is written, its planner checks Decided "Rooms" and "Room data" against its outline and reconcile rules, so a wall tool's reconcile neither rewrites nor duplicates the benchmark rooms; G2 fails at build if the room keys differ. (f) P205's note that 205a updates the generator's room literals no longer applies: 236 builds after 205a against version 3.

## 10. Open questions
None open.
- Q-0587 (answered-agent): (a) the `open.cold` row of `project-open-ms` stays pending for EZD-237; giving the perf check a database is build-system work, frozen by CLAUDE.md rule 18. No step here changes (Decided "`open.cold`").

# EZD-207 · Plan canvas (split proposal)

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-207-1 … AC-EZD-207-10 (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:714-723`, stage-0), shared out to the parts below
- **Complexity:** high (parts a and b), medium (part c); reasons per part
- **Areas:** ui, testing, canvas, performance
- **User-visible result:** the Plan tab draws the project's walls on a grid in their status colour. Josh pans with space-drag, right-drag or two fingers, zooms toward the cursor, uses Zoom in, Zoom out and Fit, and sees the wall under the cursor highlighted and room labels on the plan (a, b). The performance check pans and zooms the 3,000-object benchmark plan at desktop and iPad size and fails on any React commit (c).
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-05 · Status: split proposal

## Split proposal

**Why.** Planned whole, the ticket touches about 45 files and needs about 50 tests. That is over the size rule (PROCESS.md section 6 "Ticket size": about 20 files, about 25 tests; Josh 2026-10-22). Sources of the count (all read 2026-11-05):
- the ticket row (`vault/tickets/phases/phase-02.md:13`) and AC-EZD-207-1 to -10;
- **dependencies to install.** No `three` or `@react-three/fiber` is in `app/package.json` yet. Their rows are already pinned in ARCH Dependencies: `three` 0.186.1, `@react-three/fiber` 9.8.2, and `@types/three` 0.186.0 (Used in: spikes only, so the row changes). `eslint-rules/boundaries.mjs:42-43` already allows `three` and `@react-three/` in `app/src/editor/`;
- **rendering.** The drawing list (P238 `buildDrawingList(document, view, dimensions)`, `DrawingItem` kinds line, arc, fill, hatch and text) becomes merged geometry: one line buffer per layer and one glyph atlas for all text. This is 11 rule 4 and the EZD-027 carry-over (`vault/spikes/EZD-027.md:40`: 0 buffers rebuilt on pan, 0 idle renders, about 21 draw calls). Text has two fonts once EZD-205a lands: DM Mono 400 (P238) and Instrument Sans 600 for the room label (P205 part a);
- **input.** Zoom toward the cursor (wheel, trackpad pinch, touch pinch) and pan (space-drag, right-drag, two-finger drag) (S03 Canvas interactions). All of it runs with no React render per pointer event (11 rule 4; ARCH Editor shell).
- **zoom stack.** It needs two icons not yet in `app/src/components/icon/icons.json` (`remove`, `fit_screen`; `add` is there). That means the icon pipeline files plus `HeaderButton.icon.test.tsx`, which pins the icon list (lesson L-021);
- **hover.** Hover uses EZD-206's `WallSnapIndex` (P206 seam "EZD-207 hover"; Q-0563). The `showObject` seam for the conflict-row Show button belongs here too (Q-0511 (b), Q-0568);
- **performance check.** It needs a benchmark page that runs with no database. The perf check starts `next start` with no Supabase env (ARCH Performance check), and P236 "dependents" says "207: `generateBenchmarkModel()` in memory". The check also needs:
  - a 3-second pan **and zoom** (`scripts/perf/pan-script.mjs` today does two drag sweeps of about 2.9 s, with no zoom);
  - an iPad-size profile with CPU throttling (`scripts/perf/perf.config.mjs` `PROFILES` has `desktop` only; P017 G12: "the iPad-throttled and Surface profiles are EZD-207's");
  - the `frame.ipad` trend row (`scripts/perf/budgets.mjs`, present but unused);
  - edits to the EZD-017 tests that pin profiles and config.

The work splits into three lettered parts, built a → b → c. A dependency on EZD-207 (EZD-208, 209, 216, 223, 224, 231, 235, 237) means all three parts (`vault/tickets/README.md`, split rule). Each part is planned as its own unit from its section here.

### Part EZD-207a · Plan canvas: renderer, drawing, grid, pan and zoom
- **Scope (renderer):**
  - One persistent React Three Fiber canvas and WebGL renderer for the whole editor, drawn on demand (`frameloop` demand). The Plan scene is drawn into it; later tabs add their scenes to the same canvas and never create or destroy a context (11 rule 4; 02 Stack 2D + 3D; ticket Scope). It is mounted once in the frame's canvas region by EZD-120c's `ProjectEditor` (`app/src/editor/ProjectEditor.tsx`, P120c step 6) when the session is `ready`.
  - Code lives in `app/src/editor/plan/` (reserved for the canvas by `boundaries.mjs:11`).
  - The device pixel ratio cap is decided in part a's plan. EZD-027 measured at 1x (`EZD-027.md:40`); part c measures a high-density screen.
- **Scope (drawing):**
  - The scene draws from `buildDrawingList` (P238) for the open floor: lines, arcs, fills and hatches. Geometry is merged per drawing layer, item kind and line-weight role, with no object per wall (11 rule 4). Text items are part b's.
  - Status colours per drawing layer come from board S03's Phase rows (`html/project/S03Plan.dc.html:82-84`): `existing` `--ez-slate-400`, `demo` `--ez-red`, `new` `--ez-cobalt`. Every phase 4 wall is Existing (Q-0558).
  - WebGL needs numbers, so the token values in `app/src/styles/tokens.ts` (`TOKENS`) are converted to sRGB by a pure function, hex and `oklch()` both. `--ez-cobalt` and `--ez-red` are `oklch()`.
  - Buffers are rebuilt only when the model or floor changes, never on pan or zoom (11 rules 2 and 4).
- **Scope (grid):**
  - The grid is drawn in model units on the canvas and moves with pan and zoom. Part a's plan decides its meaning (Q-0568 "plans decide grid meaning"). Board S03 has 32 px squares of `--ez-canvas-grid` on `--ez-canvas` (`S03Plan.dc.html:47`), and at the board's 100% zoom a square is about 1 ft.
  - Part a's plan also decides how the WebGL grid meets the frame root's CSS grid. ARCH Editor shell: "The grid is CSS on the frame root until EZD-207 decides how its WebGL grid meets it".
- **Scope (camera and input):**
  - The orthographic camera zooms toward the cursor on wheel and trackpad pinch (wheel with ctrl), and on a two-pointer touch pinch. It pans on space-drag, right-drag and two-finger drag (S03 Canvas interactions).
  - Input listeners on the canvas element change the camera and call the R3F invalidate. They set no React state. Readouts that change per pointer move use refs (ARCH Editor shell; 11 rule 4).
  - Part a's plan decides zoom limits, the zoom factor per wheel step, what 100% means, the first view on open (Fit), and Fit on an empty model (Q-0568 "plans decide … zoom limits, Fit on an empty model"). Fit itself (the model's bounds plus a margin) is camera math in part a; the Fit button is part b's.
- **Scope (seams for dependents):** part a's section 3 gives these as one canvas handle that `ProjectEditor` passes on, each read or called synchronously inside a pointer handler with no React state (11 rule 4; ARCH Editor shell). Part a's plan names the handle and its members.
  - `getCursor(): { x: number; y: number } | null`, read from the input controller's ref: CSS px from the canvas region's top-left, `null` before the first pointer event (P209 C17 props; P209 section 9 note "`getCursor` from the canvas input controller's ref"). EZD-210b passes it to `TypedEntryLayer`.
  - `pixelsPerInch`, the camera's current screen px per model inch, a finite number above 0 (P206 seam "EZD-210 Wall tool": `pixelsPerInch` from the camera; P206 `SnapRequest.pixelsPerInch`).
  - Model-to-screen and screen-to-model transforms for a point (model inches, +x east, +y north, P203 Decided Axes; screen CSS px as `getCursor`) (P210 Ledger notes; P210 part b Scope (pointer and overlay)).
  - A camera-change callback that runs outside React on every pan or zoom, with an unsubscribe (P210 Ledger notes), so EZD-210b's overlay and P209's box follow the view.
  - A pointer hand-off: the active tool registers one receiver and gets left click, double-click, drag and move in model inches; space-drag, right-drag and two-finger drag stay with the canvas and never reach it (P210 Ledger notes; S03 Canvas interactions). With no receiver registered, left input does nothing in part a.
- **Scope (shell, states, permissions):**
  - Header `views={['plan']}`, so the Plan tab shows (Q-0568; `EditorHeader` `views` prop, `components/shell/editor-views.ts`).
  - No left panel or inspector, and the status bar shows the disclaimer only (Q-0568; P120c Frame row).
  - Loading keeps P120c's skeleton (Q-0214; Q-0506).
  - A canvas that cannot start (no WebGL, context creation throws) shows an inline message with Retry in the canvas region (Q-0214; Q-0568; `components/states` `InlineError`, EZD-015).
  - A user without Edit model gets the same canvas, pan and zoom (S03 Permissions; Q-0568).
  - No rail and no typed bar exist yet. The Wall and Room rectangle rail entries come with EZD-210, the bar with EZD-209 (Q-0500: a control appears when its ticket ships). Part a tests that a loading or view-only editor shows neither (rail region absent).
  - The S03 "Empty" hint is not built here. Q-0500 applies it once the grid and the tools ship, so EZD-221 (templates, the last of them) adds it.
- **Done when:**
  - AC-EZD-207-1 and AC-EZD-207-9, verbatim.
  - AC-EZD-207-4 for lines, arcs, fills and hatches.
  - AC-EZD-207-6 except "tools are disabled": while the model loads the canvas shows a skeleton; if the canvas cannot start it shows an inline message with Retry.
  - AC-EZD-207-7 except "a rail with Wall and Room rectangle": the editor shows the Plan tab, no left panel or inspector, and the status bar's disclaimer only.
  - The two excepted clauses are EZD-210b's: part a builds no rail and no tools (Q-0500), and P210 part b builds the rail with Wall and Room rectangle and disables the tools while loading (P210 part b Scope (mount), Scope (permissions and states), Tests). The orchestrator records them against EZD-210b in TRACE.md.
  - AC-EZD-207-8 for pan and zoom.
  - Then: a scroll at a point keeps the model point under the cursor where it was. A pan or zoom rebuilds no geometry buffer and makes no React commit (EZD-027 carry-over; 11 rule 4). With nothing changing, no frame is drawn (ticket Scope).
  - Section 3 lists every member of Scope (seams for dependents) with its signature, and each has a test: `getCursor` after a pointer move; `pixelsPerInch` at two zooms; the two transforms round-trip a point at a panned and zoomed camera; the camera-change callback fires once per camera change and not after unsubscribe; a registered receiver gets left click, double-click, drag and move in model inches and never a space-drag, right-drag or two-finger drag.
- **Depends on:**
  - from the row: EZD-012 (a, b, c), EZD-202, EZD-238, EZD-017, EZD-020;
  - missing from the row: EZD-120c (the editor route and `ProjectEditor` this mounts into; reached only through EZD-236 → EZD-120), EZD-015 (`InlineError`, done), EZD-016a (browser harness, for the visual checklist; done), EZD-027 (spike carry-overs; done).
- **Files (about 18):**
  - `app/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `docs/architecture.md` (the `@types/three` row's Used in; new `### Plan canvas (EZD-207)`; the Editor shell grid line);
  - `app/src/editor/plan/`: colour conversion, camera and grid math, drawing-list batches, input controller (each with a test file), `PlanCanvas.tsx` and its CSS;
  - `app/src/editor/ProjectEditor.tsx` and the earlier-test edit to P120c B2 (it expects 0 header nav buttons and canvas text "");
  - `app/src/server/messages/catalogs/en.ts` (the canvas start failure message);
  - one Playwright spec (`app/e2e/`).
- **Tests (about 20):**
  - zoom about a point keeps that point fixed; zoom limits clamp; pan by a screen delta; Fit of a bounds with margin; Fit of an empty model;
  - grid step at several zooms;
  - hex and `oklch()` token conversion (expected values from the CSS Color 4 OKLab formulas);
  - batches: one geometry per (layer, kind, role); vertex counts from a fixture list; layer colours; no rebuild on camera change;
  - controller: wheel, ctrl-wheel, right-drag, space-drag, plain left drag (no pan), two-pointer drag and pinch, each with the invalidate count;
  - seams: `getCursor`, `pixelsPerInch`, transform round trip, camera-change callback and unsubscribe, pointer hand-off with pan gestures kept (Done when);
  - browser: walls in Existing grey at a known pixel; no frames while idle; 0 React commits across a pan; view-only pans; a WebGL failure shows the message and Retry; Plan tab shown, no left panel, inspector or rail.
- **Complexity:** high. It is the editor's performance core: a new WebGL renderer, merged buffers and input with no React renders, which every later drawing ticket builds on (PROCESS.md section 4; Slice 4 Risks). Test-author Sonnet 5.5, builder Opus 5.5.
- **security-review: no.** The canvas reads the model already loaded by P120c and `viewer.canEdit`. It adds no route, table, policy, permission or money field.
- **Reviewers:** code-reviewer · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier yes · security-reviewer no.
- **Visual checklist:** yes, desktop 1600 × 1000. Rows: grid; walls in each status colour; canvas failure message; view-only (filled).
- **Proposed wording:** the canvas start failure message (part a's plan proposes it in the Q-0214 style; Josh approves at Stage 2).

### Part EZD-207b · Plan canvas: zoom stack, hover and text
- **Scope (zoom stack):**
  - Zoom in, Zoom out and Fit to screen at the top right of the canvas. They step the zoom about the canvas centre and fit the model (S03 Canvas interactions; 00e Zoom stack).
  - Board S03 (`S03Plan.dc.html:137-141`):
    - the stack is a column 16 px from the top and right, white, with a 1 px `--ez-border` border and radius 10;
    - each button is 38 × 38, with icons `add`, `remove` and `fit_screen` at 20 px in `--ez-slate-700`;
    - the dividers are `--ez-divider`;
    - the aria-labels are "Zoom in", "Zoom out" and "Fit to screen".
  - 11 Accessibility requires touch targets of at least 44 px on the iPad (`--ez-touch-target`), and the board's buttons are 38 px. Part b's plan reconciles the two from the device-layout precedent (EZD-014) or raises a QP.
  - `remove` and `fit_screen` go through the icon pipeline (EZD-010b), with the `HeaderButton.icon.test.tsx` list edit (L-021).
- **Scope (hover):**
  - With no tool active, the wall under the cursor is highlighted (Q-0570, replacing Q-0568's hover line).
  - The lookup goes through EZD-206's `WallSnapIndex.spatial.query(rect)` and `getWall(id)`, kept current with `upsertWall` / `removeWall` per changed wall (P206 seam; Q-0563; 11 rule 4).
  - The highlight geometry changes only when the hovered id changes. Part b's plan decides the hover style (Q-0568 "plans decide … hover style").
  - The canvas exposes a hover mode (`wall` or `off`). EZD-210 sets `off` while a drawing tool is active and `wall` in pick mode, which EZD-210 names (00e Pick mode; Q-0570). Hover works without Edit model (S03 Permissions; Q-0568).
  - Seams for EZD-210b (P210 Ledger notes; P210 part b Scope (pointer and overlay)), added to part a's canvas handle and listed in part b's section 3 with signatures: the hover-mode setter (`wall` | `off`), and the hovered wall id (`string | null`, `null` over empty space or with mode `off`), read synchronously inside a pointer handler so pick mode picks the highlighted wall (AC-EZD-207-3 "the wall a click would pick").
- **Scope (text):**
  - Drawing-list text items are drawn as instanced quads from one glyph atlas for all fonts (11 rule 4; EZD-027 carry-over: a 512 × 512 DM Mono atlas). Those items are dimension text (P238, `dm-mono-400`) and the room label `NAME · N SF` (Q-0576 (a): EZD-205 adds it to the list; P205 part a: Instrument Sans 600).
  - The glyphs come from the self-hosted fonts (11 rule 8; `app/src/styles/fonts.ts`).
  - Part b's plan decides how `sizePt` becomes screen size at a given zoom. S03 Text: "Prints at fixed paper size at any scale"; the board's label is 15 px at 100%.
- **Scope (Show seam):**
  - `showObject(id)` zooms and centres the view on one object's bounds (Q-0511 (b)).
  - EZD-299 is blocked (STATUS; Q-0567), so it will be built second and adds the conflict-row Show button that calls this (Q-0568).
  - If EZD-299 is built before part b is planned, part b adds the button instead (AC-EZD-207-10).
- **Done when:**
  - AC-EZD-207-2 and AC-EZD-207-3, verbatim.
  - AC-EZD-207-8 for Fit and hover.
  - AC-EZD-207-4 for text items.
  - AC-EZD-207-10 as its seam: `showObject(id)` frames the object, and the button is added by whichever of EZD-207b and EZD-299 is built second (Q-0568).
  - Then: hovering a wall changes the highlight with no React commit, and all text on the plan comes from one atlas texture.
  - Section 3 lists the hover-mode setter and the hovered wall id on the canvas handle, each with a test: mode `off` clears the highlight and the id reads `null`; mode `wall` over a wall reads that wall's id inside a pointer handler.
- **Depends on:**
  - from the row: EZD-207a, EZD-206;
  - missing from the row: EZD-205 (part a: the room label in the drawing list and its font; it is already earlier in the Slice 4 build order), EZD-010b (icon pipeline; done), EZD-016a.
- **Files (about 16):**
  - `ZoomStack.tsx` and its CSS;
  - `icons.json`, two SVGs, `public/icons/sprite.svg`, `icon-names.generated.ts`, `HeaderButton.icon.test.tsx` (test-author edit);
  - `en.ts` if the aria-label keys are new;
  - in `app/src/editor/plan/`: hover and glyph-atlas modules, each with a test file; batch and controller changes;
  - one Playwright spec;
  - `docs/architecture.md` (the Plan canvas section).
  - Part b's plan greps the earlier tests that read canvas-region text or count buttons (lesson EZD-136 plan-gap) and names each edit.
- **Tests (about 18):**
  - zoom step in and out and its limits; Fit button;
  - hover: wall under the cursor, none over empty space, change only on a new id, mode `off`, the index query count (not a scan);
  - atlas: one texture for both fonts, glyph quad count equals the text length, size at two zooms;
  - `showObject` bounds; browser checks of the stack, hover highlight pixels and room label presence.
- **Complexity:** high. Glyph-atlas text in WebGL with two fonts, and hover on the shared index, both under the no-render rule (PROCESS.md section 4). Test-author Sonnet 5.5, builder Opus 5.5.
- **security-review: no.** UI only; no route, table, permission or money field.
- **Reviewers:** code-reviewer · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier yes · security-reviewer no.
- **Visual checklist:** yes, desktop 1600 × 1000. Rows: zoom stack (board measures above); hover highlight; room label.
- **Proposed wording:** none expected; the three button labels are on the board.

### Part EZD-207c · Benchmark pan and zoom in the performance check
- **Scope (page):**
  - A developer page under `app/src/app/dev/` (`notFound()` in production, ARCH Folder layout; `boundaries.mjs:18` lets `app/src/app/dev/` import editor code). It opens the plan canvas on `generateBenchmarkModel()` in memory (P236 section 3 dependents), with no database.
  - `scripts/perf/perf.config.mjs` `panUrl` is repointed to it. The registry owner text reads "EZD-207 adds the benchmark project" (`scripts/perf/registry.mjs`).
- **Scope (gesture):**
  - The scripted gesture becomes a 3-second pan and zoom: the existing right-drag and space-drag sweeps plus wheel zoom steps (ticket Done-when; P017 P2 pattern).
  - Setup moves stay before `pan-start` (lesson EZD-017 round 2).
- **Scope (profiles):**
  - A second profile at iPad size, 1180 × 820 (Q-0053; Q-0088), with CPU throttling through Chromium's DevTools protocol.
  - The throttle rate has no source yet (read: 11 Performance, P017, Q-0061, Q-0097). Part c's plan finds one or raises it as a QP.
  - The pan runs under both profiles. `react-commits.pan` (gate, 0) and `long-tasks.pan` (gate, 0, Q-0073 (a)) apply to each profile. Part c's plan says whether the throttled run keeps the long-task gate or records it as a trend.
  - Frame times join as trends: `frame.desktop`, `frame.ipad`, `frame.max` (Q-0061 (a); Phase 4 Build gate line, "frame times are a trend, not a gate").
  - EZD-027's carry-over asks for a high-density check (`deviceScaleFactor` 2 on the iPad profile; part c's plan decides).
- **Scope (draw calls):** `draw-calls-per-frame` (owner EZD-207, budget `null`, P017 G9) stays `pending` unless a source gives a number. EZD-027's "about 21 draw calls" is a spike measurement, not a budget. Part c's plan either keeps it pending with that reason or raises a QP.
- **Done when:** AC-EZD-207-5, verbatim. Then: the perf check fails on purpose when the probe adds one commit per pointer move on the benchmark page under each profile (P017 H1 probe pattern), and `perf-results/latest.json` holds the iPad-size frame statistics.
- **Depends on:**
  - from the row: EZD-207b, EZD-236, EZD-017;
  - missing from the row: EZD-120c (through EZD-236; the page reuses no route).
- **Files (about 12):**
  - the dev page and its client component and test;
  - `scripts/perf/perf.config.mjs`, `pan-script.mjs`, `check.mjs` or `run.mjs`, `registry.mjs`;
  - the EZD-017 tests that pin `PROFILES`, the config and registry rows (T13 and the wiring tests; part c's plan names each with its new value, lesson EZD-020);
  - `docs/architecture.md` `### Performance check (EZD-017)`.
- **Tests (about 12):**
  - the page renders the benchmark model with no Supabase env;
  - gesture timing (3 s) and its wheel steps;
  - both profiles run, with throttling applied;
  - the commit probe fails under each profile;
  - trend rows recorded and never failing;
  - the config and registry pins.
- **Complexity:** medium. It extends the EZD-017 harness and its patterns, with one new browser-protocol call (PROCESS.md section 4). Test-author Sonnet 5.5, builder Sonnet 5.5.
- **security-review: no.** A dev page that is 404 in production, plus perf scripts; no route, table or permission.
- **Reviewers:** code-reviewer · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer no.
- **Visual checklist:** none (dev page for measurement only).
- **Proposed wording:** none (a dev page with no user text).

### Notes for the orchestrator
- Apply the split as for EZD-205: phase file rows, `tickets.json` entries, and `acs` per part as listed in each Done when. AC-EZD-207-4 and AC-EZD-207-8 are shared by a and b. AC-EZD-207-6 and AC-EZD-207-7 are shared by part a and EZD-210b: TRACE.md records the "tools are disabled" and "a rail with Wall and Room rectangle" clauses against EZD-210b (part a Done when; review-phase-04 item 5).
- EZD-221's planner adds the S03 "Empty" hint (Q-0500); EZD-221's row does not say so.
- EZD-209 and EZD-210's planners must keep the bar and tools hidden without Edit model and disabled while loading (AC-EZD-207-6, -8 clauses that land with them; Q-0568).
- EZD-210 sets the canvas hover mode for its tools and pick mode (part b seam). EZD-210b's other needs (`getCursor`, `pixelsPerInch`, transforms, camera-change callback, pointer hand-off) are part a's seams; the hovered wall id is part b's (review-phase-04 item 4).

## Open questions
None at the split. Each part's plan raises its own: part a's on the grid, zoom limits and pixel ratio if no source decides them; part b's on touch target size and text scaling; part c's on the throttle rate and the draw-call budget.

# EZD-209 · Typed dimension bar

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-209-1, AC-EZD-209-2, AC-EZD-209-3, AC-EZD-209-4, AC-EZD-209-5 (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:724-728`, stage-0)
- **Complexity:** medium (section 8)
- **Areas:** ui, testing
- **User-visible result:** with a drawing tool active, a bar at the bottom center of the plan shows the tool, its field and the last wall's length; typing a number opens a small box at the cursor where Josh types `12'6"`, Tab, `90`, Enter; a bad entry shows the accepted formats and the box stays open. Josh sees it on the test page `/dev/typed-bar` now and in the Wall and Room rectangle tools when EZD-210 ships.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-05 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build

No data, tables or migrations. Three parts: a pure turn-angle module in the geometry package (AC-4), a pure typed-entry reducer plus a React layer in `app/src/editor/typed-entry/` (AC-1, 2, 3, 5), and a stub-tool test page. The layer is not mounted in the real editor: EZD-210 mounts it with the first real tools (Q-0570 "The typed bar shows only with a tool active"; Q-0500 a control appears when its ticket ships; section 9).

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `packages/geometry/src/turn.ts` | new | C1–C5 (section 3); algorithm D-Turn, D-Angle | EZD-201's `packages/geometry/src/length.ts` (pure, `{ ok } \| { ok: false … }` result, message key const), merged before this build (`depends_on`); the plain-module shape is also in `app/src/components/states/toast-store.ts` | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry test` (G1–G4) |
| 2 | `packages/geometry/src/index.ts` | change | append `export * from './turn';` as the last line; change nothing else | the file itself (EZD-201 E10 line) | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry typecheck` |
| 3 | `app/src/server/messages/catalogs/en.ts` | change | the 6 keys of section 6, one block directly after the `'office.length.refused'` entry (EZD-201 E11; EZD-201 merges first, `depends_on`; if that entry is missing, stop with PLAN-GAP), in section 6 order; nothing else | existing `office.` entries | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app typecheck` |
| 4 | `app/src/editor/typed-entry/typed-entry.ts` | new | C6–C16 (section 3); rules D-Open … D-Esc | `app/src/components/states/toast-store.ts` (plain module, no React, typed state) | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec vitest run src/editor/typed-entry` (R1–R7) |
| 5 | `app/src/editor/typed-entry/TypedEntryLayer.module.css` | new | classes of D-CSS, exactly | `app/src/components/shell/ToolRail.module.css` (tokens, coarse-pointer block) | B1 computed styles |
| 6 | `app/src/editor/typed-entry/TypedEntryLayer.tsx` | new | `'use client'`; C17–C19 | `app/src/components/shell/ToolRail.tsx` (client component, `useT()`, `Icon`) | M1–M3, B1–B5 |
| 7 | `app/src/app/dev/typed-bar/page.module.css` | new | `.stage` (position absolute; inset 0), `.toggle` (position absolute; left 16px; top 16px; z-index 2), `.log` (position absolute; left 16px; top 56px; z-index 2; margin 0; font-family var(--ez-font-mono); font-size 12px); nothing else | `app/src/app/dev/states/page.module.css` | B1 |
| 8 | `app/src/app/dev/typed-bar/TypedBarDemo.tsx` | new | `'use client'`; `export function TypedBarDemo({ canEdit }: { canEdit: boolean })`; D-Demo | `app/src/components/shell/EmptyEditor.tsx` (EditorFrame with empty ToolRail and StatusBar) | B1–B5 |
| 9 | `app/src/app/dev/typed-bar/page.tsx` | new | `export default async function Page({ searchParams }: { searchParams: Promise<{ edit?: string \| string[] }> })` | `app/src/app/dev/states/page.tsx` (production `notFound()`), `app/src/app/dev/shell/page.tsx` (office catalog) | P1, P2 |
| 10 | `docs/architecture.md` | change | new `### Typed dimension bar (EZD-209)` directly after `### Editor shell (EZD-012)`: files, C17 props, the key rule of D-Keys (capture listener; handled keys stop propagation and are `defaultPrevented`), `isTypingTarget` for tool shortcuts, `/dev/typed-bar`; 5 bullets, nothing else | `### Editor shell (EZD-012)` | review only (L-041: no test reads it) |
| 11 | test files (test-author) | new | `packages/geometry/src/turn.test.ts`, `app/src/editor/typed-entry/typed-entry.test.ts`, `app/src/editor/typed-entry/TypedEntryLayer.test.tsx`, `app/src/app/dev/typed-bar/page.test.tsx`, `app/e2e/typed-bar.spec.ts` | section 4 | `node scripts/gate.mjs .claude/worktrees/EZD-209` |

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D-Angle parse | `parseTurnAngle(text)`: `s = text.trim()`; `s.length === 0` or `s.length > 16` → refused; `s` must match `/^\d+(?:\.\d+)?$/` else refused; `n = Number(s)`; `n < 180` → `{ ok: true, degrees: n }`, else refused. Refused = `{ ok: false, messageKey: TURN_REFUSED_MESSAGE_KEY }`. No `°`, sign, exponent or leading `.` is accepted. Never throws. | Q-0570 (0 up to but not including 180, decimals as typed; 180, above and negatives refused); 16-char bound: CLAUDE.md rule 18, EZD-201 D2 pattern |
| D-Turn | `resolveTurnDirection({ previous, toCursor, turnDeg })`, `c = toCursor`: (1) `turnDeg === null`: `len = Math.hypot(c.x, c.y)`; `len === 0` → `null`; else `{ x: c.x/len, y: c.y/len }`. (2) else `ref` = `previous` normalized when `previous !== null` and its length > 0; otherwise `{ x: c.x < 0 ? -1 : 1, y: 0 }`. `cross = ref.x*c.y - ref.y*c.x`; `s = cross < 0 ? -1 : 1`; `a = s*turnDeg*Math.PI/180`; return `{ x: ref.x*Math.cos(a) - ref.y*Math.sin(a), y: ref.x*Math.sin(a) + ref.y*Math.cos(a) }`. Works in either y direction: the turn always goes to the cursor's side of `ref`. It does not validate `turnDeg` (callers pass a `parseTurnAngle` result). | Q-0560 (turn from the last wall; cursor side picks left or right; nothing typed → where the cursor points); Q-0570 (first wall from the page's horizontal); 09j Turn angle rows 1–5 |
| Snapping | Not here. `toCursor` is already snapped by the caller (EZD-210 with EZD-206). | Q-0570 ("where the cursor points" means after snapping) |
| D-Fields | `WALL_LENGTH_FIELD` = `{ id: 'length', label: 'office.typed.field.length', kind: 'length', lengthKind: 'wall_room', optional: false }`; `TURN_ANGLE_FIELD` = `{ id: 'angle', label: 'office.typed.field.angle', kind: 'angle', optional: true }`. EZD-210 reuses them. | S03 Tab (Length → Angle); Q-0560 (angle may be left empty); Q-0570 (wall field limits) |
| D-Validate | One field's text `t`: `t.trim() === ''` → optional: value `null`; required: refused with `LENGTH_REFUSED_MESSAGE_KEY` (length) or `TURN_REFUSED_MESSAGE_KEY` (angle). Else length → `parseLength(t, field.lengthKind)` (EZD-201 E7; refusal key is its `messageKey`); angle → `parseTurnAngle(t)`. | 04 Measurement entry; Q-0561 (refusal message); EZD-201 E3 |
| D-Open | `{ type: 'open', text, anchor }` when closed: `open: true`, `active: 0`, `texts` = `text` at index 0 and `''` elsewhere, `error: null`, `anchor` as given; `handled: true`. When already open it acts as `append`. | 04 Measurement entry ("typing a number opens an inline length box"); S03 Tab |
| D-Edit | `edit` sets `texts[active]` to `text` and `error` to `null`; `append` adds `text` to the end of `texts[active]` and sets `error` to `null`. Both `handled: false` and no change when closed. | (reducer rule) |
| D-Tab | `tab` when open: if `texts[active]` is not empty and refused → stay, `error` = its key. Otherwise `active` = `(active + 1) % n`, or `(active - 1 + n) % n` when `back`, `error: null`. A one-field tool stays on field 0. `handled: true`. Closed → `handled: false`, no change. | S03 Tab ("moves to the next field") |
| D-Enter | `enter` when open: validate fields in order; first refused field → `active` = its index, `error` = its key, `open` stays `true`, no commit. All pass → `commit` = object with every field id → value (`number \| null`); new state = closed initial state (D-Init). `handled: true`. Closed → `handled: false`. | 04 Measurement entry (Enter commits); AC-5 (field stays open) |
| D-Esc | `escape` when open → closed initial state, `handled: true`, no commit. Closed → `handled: false` (the tool's own Esc runs: Q-0568 segment cancel, then no tool). | S03 Esc ("Cancels current operation"); Q-0568 |
| D-Init | `initialTypedEntryState(tool)` = `{ open: false, active: 0, texts: tool.fields.map(() => ''), error: null, anchor: 'cursor' }`. | (reducer rule) |
| D-Keys | The layer adds one `keydown` listener on `window` with `{ capture: true }`, only while `tool !== null && canEdit`. Event target is the box input → do nothing (the input's handler runs). Closed: `isOpenKey(e)` and not `isTypingTarget(e.target)` → `preventDefault()`, `stopPropagation()`, dispatch `open` with `text: e.key`, `anchor: 'cursor'`. Open (target not the input, not a typing target): a digit (`isOpenKey`) → `append`, then focus the input; `Tab` (with `shiftKey` → back), `Enter`, `Escape` → that action. Every key the listener acts on gets `preventDefault()` and `stopPropagation()`; others pass untouched. The input's `onKeyDown`: `Tab`, `Enter`, `Escape` → `preventDefault()`, `stopPropagation()`, dispatch; any other key → `stopPropagation()` only (so tool shortcuts never fire while typing). | 04 Measurement entry; S03 Enter, Tab, Esc; contract for EZD-210 (section 3 C17) |
| Focus | When `open` turns true, a layout effect focuses the input. Blur never closes the box; only Enter (commit) and Esc close it. | 04 (Enter commits); S03 Esc |
| D-State | `useState` holding `TypedEntryState` plus a ref mirror. Every handler computes `step = reduceTypedEntry(tool, ref.current, action)` synchronously, sets the ref and state, then calls `onCommit(step.commit)` when non-null, outside any state updater, so one Enter calls `onCommit` exactly once (also under React StrictMode). | ticket Done-when ("emits one commit") |
| Tool change | The layer renders its inner part with `key={tool.id}`, so a new tool, or the tool going null and back, starts from D-Init. | (state rule) |
| Hidden | `tool === null` or `canEdit === false` → the layer renders nothing (no root element) and registers no listener. | Q-0570 (bar only with a tool active); Q-0568 (without Edit model the bar is hidden) |
| D-Pos | Box position, set in a layout effect when `open` turns true (not on Tab), written to `box.style.left` / `.top` in px, no extra render. `W, H` = root `clientWidth/clientHeight`; `w, h` = box `offsetWidth/offsetHeight`. Anchor `cursor` with `p = getCursor()` not null: `left = max(8, min(p.x + 12, W - w - 8))`, `top = max(8, min(p.y + 12, H - h - 8))`. Anchor `bar`, or `p === null`: `left = round((W - w) / 2)`, `top = bar.offsetTop - h - 8`. `getCursor` is called only here; the layer adds no pointer listener. | 04 ("at the cursor"); 11 Performance rule 4 (no React render per pointer event); offsets 12 and 8: layout detail with no rule (tickets README rule 5) |
| Touch | The chip is a `<button>`; pressing it when closed dispatches `open` with `text: ''`, `anchor: 'bar'`; when open it only focuses the input. Its class list adds `touch.hitArea` from `app/src/styles/touch.module.css`, giving a 44 px hit area on coarse pointers without changing the board look. Input attributes: `type="text"`, `inputMode="text"`, `autoComplete="off"`, `autoCorrect="off"`, `autoCapitalize="off"`, `spellCheck={false}`, `maxLength={32}`, `aria-label` = field label, `aria-invalid` = `error !== null`. | S03 Live distance chips ("Click a chip to type an exact distance"); 11 Accessibility (44 px); Q-0053 (iPad); EZD-201 D2 (32 chars) |
| D-Bar content | Field = `tool.fields[state.active]`. Chip: `Icon name={tool.icon} size={16}`, label `t(field.label)`, value span only when `field.kind === 'length'` and `lastValues[field.id]` is defined: `formatLength(v, PLAN_DISPLAY_DENOMINATOR)`. Then `error !== null` → error span `t(error)`, `role="alert"`; else hint span `t('office.typed.hint_length')` (length field) or `t('office.typed.hint_angle')` (angle field). Tab chip `t('office.typed.tab')` only when `tool.fields.length > 1`. | board S03 lines 132–135; Q-0564 (last wall's length); Q-0561 (no laser, so the board hint loses "or use the laser"); 03g / EZD-201 E6 (plans at 1/2") |
| D-Box content | Box: label span `t(field.label)` above the input; input value `texts[active]`; `onChange` → `edit`. | board S03 `.fl` / `.fl input` (lines 37–38), nearest board element (tickets README rule 5) |
| D-CSS | Literal px only for sizes and spacing (no spacing tokens, L-013); every colour, radius, shadow and font from tokens. `.root` position absolute; inset 0; pointer-events none; z-index 1. `.bar` position absolute; left 50%; bottom 20px; transform translateX(-50%); display flex; align-items center; gap 12px; padding 6px 14px 6px 6px; font-size 14px; white-space nowrap; background var(--ez-surface); border 1px solid var(--ez-border); border-radius var(--ez-radius-12); box-shadow var(--ez-shadow-floating); pointer-events auto. `.chip` display flex; align-items center; gap 8px; padding 7px 12px; margin 0; border 0; background var(--ez-ink); color var(--ez-surface); border-radius var(--ez-radius-8); font: inherit; cursor pointer. `.chipLabel` font-size 13px; font-weight 500. `.chipValue` font-family var(--ez-font-mono); padding-left 8px; border-left 1px solid var(--ez-slate-700). `.hint` color var(--ez-slate-500). `.error` color var(--ez-red). `.tab` font-family var(--ez-font-mono); font-size 12px; color var(--ez-slate-500); border 1px solid var(--ez-border); border-radius var(--ez-radius-5); padding 2px 6px. `.box` position absolute; left 0; top 0; display flex; flex-direction column; gap 5px; padding 8px; font-size 12px; color var(--ez-slate-500); background var(--ez-surface); border 1px solid var(--ez-border); border-radius var(--ez-radius-8); box-shadow var(--ez-shadow-floating); pointer-events auto. `.boxInput` box-sizing border-box; width 120px; padding 9px 10px; font-family var(--ez-font-mono); font-size 14px; font-weight 400; color var(--ez-ink); background var(--ez-surface); border 1px solid var(--ez-border); border-radius var(--ez-radius-8). `.boxInput[aria-invalid='true']` border-color var(--ez-red). Nothing else; the bar does not compose `card.module.css`, because its shadow differs from `.card` (board line 132 inline style). | board S03 lines 18, 37–38, 132–135; `app/src/styles/tokens.css`; 120 px fits `200' 0 1/16"` in DM Mono 14 px plus padding |
| D-Demo | `TypedBarDemo` renders `EditorFrame` with `header={<HeaderCard />}`, `rail={<ToolRail top={[]} bottom={[]} activeId={null} onSelect={noop} />}`, `leftPanelLabel="office.shell.left_panel"`, `inspectorLabel="office.shell.inspector"`, `statusBar={<StatusBar />}` and `canvas` = a div `.stage` (`data-testid="typed-bar-stage"`) whose `onPointerMove` and `onPointerDown` store `{ x: e.clientX - rect.left, y: e.clientY - rect.top }` (rect of the stage) in a ref; then a button `.toggle` (`stub-tool-toggle`, text `Toggle tool`) that switches the tool between `STUB_TOOL` and `null`; an `<ol className={log}>` (`stub-commits`) with one `<li>` per commit, text `JSON.stringify(values)`; a span (`stub-key-count`) showing how many `keydown` events a `window` listener in the bubble phase has seen; then `<TypedEntryLayer tool canEdit lastValues getCursor onCommit />`. `STUB_TOOL` (module const) = `{ id: 'stub', icon: 'straighten', fields: [WALL_LENGTH_FIELD, TURN_ANGLE_FIELD] }`. `onCommit` appends the log line and sets `lastValues` to the commit's non-null values. Dev-page literals are allowed (no `no-literal-ui-string` block covers `app/src/app/dev/typed-bar/`). | EZD-012b `EmptyEditor.tsx`; `eslint.config.mjs` lint blocks; `icons.json` has `straighten` (no icon added) |
| Page | `page.tsx`: `VERCEL_ENV === 'production'` → `notFound()`; `canEdit = edit !== '0'`; renders `<MessagesProvider language="en" messages={catalogFor('office', 'en')}><TypedBarDemo canEdit={canEdit} /></MessagesProvider>`. | `dev/states/page.tsx`; `dev/shell/page.tsx`; architecture Folder layout (dev pages) |

### Do not touch
`app/src/components/shell/*` and its tests; `app/src/editor/ProjectEditor.tsx` and any plan-canvas file (EZD-120c, EZD-207); `packages/geometry/src/length.ts` (EZD-201); `icons.json` and the sprite (no icon added); `app/src/styles/touch.module.css`; `eslint.config.mjs`; every existing test. No earlier test needs an edit: the catalog tests derive keys from namespaces (`catalog.test.ts`), the disclaimer inventory skips `app/src/app/dev/` (`disclaimer-pages.test.ts` U6), and no test lists dev routes.

Ticket row (`vault/tickets/phases/phase-02.md:15`): Scope: Floating bar with active tool and field; typing opens the inline length box; Tab moves to the next field; Enter commits; the bar shows the last wall's length (Q-0561, Q-0564). / Done when: With a stub tool active, typing 12'6" Tab 90 Enter emits one commit of length 150" and angle 90°. / Depends on: EZD-201, EZD-207. / Spec ref: S03 Typed dimension bar; App shell · Measurement entry.

## 2. Sources
- `vault/spec/sections/screens/S03-plan-editor.md`: Layout (bar bottom center), Canvas interactions (Typed dimension bar, Tab, Enter, Esc, Live distance chips), Validation & warnings ("Length input parse errors show accepted formats").

## 7. Security review
security-review: no. A client-side input layer and a dev page: no route, table, policy, permission or money field; the dev page is not found in production.
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer always · calc-auditor no (lengths come from EZD-201's audited parser; the turn rows are closed-form cos/sin) · ui-verifier yes · security-reviewer no.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
medium: a pure reducer and turn function plus one client component with keyboard capture, focus and positioning rules, all decided here; no renderer, data or new dependency (PROCESS.md section 4). Test-author Sonnet 5.5, builder Sonnet 5.5.

## 9. Dependencies
- From the row: EZD-201 (`parseLength`, `formatLength`, `PLAN_DISPLAY_DENOMINATOR`, `LENGTH_REFUSED_MESSAGE_KEY`, `LengthFieldKind`, the `office.length.refused` text); EZD-207 (all parts; this plan uses none of its exports, and the layer mounts over the canvas only in EZD-210).
- Missing from the row: EZD-202 (adds `@ezdraft/geometry` to `app/package.json`, P202 step 12; reached through EZD-207); EZD-012 (EditorFrame, ToolRail, HeaderCard, StatusBar for the dev page; done); EZD-010b (`Icon`; done); EZD-014b/c (`touch.module.css`, `expectTouchTargets`; done); EZD-016a (browser harness, for the visual checklist; done).
- For EZD-210's planner: mount `TypedEntryLayer` in the canvas region after the plan canvas, pass the active tool (`WALL_LENGTH_FIELD` + `TURN_ANGLE_FIELD` for Wall; Width and Depth fields for Room rectangle), `canEdit`, the last wall's length in `lastValues` (also for clicked walls, Q-0564), `getCursor` from the canvas input controller's ref, and call `resolveTurnDirection` with the snapped cursor; tool shortcuts skip `isTypingTarget` targets and `defaultPrevented` events.
- Risks: the capture listener stops handled keys before any other listener, so a later global shortcut must not need digits, Tab, Enter or Esc while the box is open. No performance budget is at risk: no pointer listener, and renders happen only on keys.

## 10. Open questions
None.

# EZD-210 · Wall and Room rectangle tools (split proposal)

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-210-1 … AC-EZD-210-12 (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:729-740`, stage-0), shared out to the parts below
- **Complexity:** high (each part; reasons per part)
- **Areas:** ui, testing, geometry, canvas
- **User-visible result:** in a project Josh presses W and draws walls by clicking and typing lengths and turns, or presses R and types a width and depth; the walls save, a closed chain becomes a room labelled `ROOM 1 · 120 SF`, a snap marker shows what the cursor caught, and a chain that misses its start by up to 12" shows a gap box with Pick the wall that absorbs it and Keep the room out of square.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-05 · Status: split proposal

## Split proposal

**Why.** Planned whole, the ticket touches about 27 files and needs about 35 tests, over the size rule (PROCESS.md section 6 "Ticket size": about 20 files, about 25 tests; Josh 2026-10-22). Sources of the count:
- the ticket row (`vault/tickets/phases/phase-02.md:16`) and AC-EZD-210-1 to -12 (12 ACs, each with a logic side and most with a screen side);
- two tool state machines (Wall chain: click, type, turn, close, double-click or Enter twice, Esc per segment; Room rectangle: corner, drag or type, grow direction) (S03 Rail tools Wall and Room rectangle; 04 Tool rail; Q-0560; Q-0568; Q-0570);
- the walls and rooms they write go through EZD-120b's model store and outbox, with EZD-205a's room reconcile step ("every wall-changing tool calls it", P205 part a);
- the gap box: derived from the walls on every load (Q-0570), three or more walls, size to 1/16", absorb only for a parallel wall, Keep out of square, pick mode with Esc back to the box, buttons hidden without Edit model (Q-0562; Q-0568; Q-0569; Q-0570; S02 Resolve the gap; 09j Closure, Absorbing a gap);
- the snap marker per snap kind (S03 Snap; Q-0563; P206 `SnapResult.kind`);
- the screen: rail entries and two icons through the icon pipeline (EZD-010b; `HeaderButton.icon.test.tsx` pins the icon list, lesson L-021), W, R and Esc keys, the mounted `TypedEntryLayer` (P209 section 9 note), pointer wiring and an overlay that redraws per pointer move with no React render (11 rule 4; ARCH Editor shell), permission and loading states (Q-0568; S03 Permissions, States), `en.ts` messages, and browser tests for Josh's Slice 4 test script steps 2, 3, 6 and 7.

**Two more reasons to cut at the logic/screen line.**
- EZD-205 and EZD-207 are split proposals whose parts are not planned yet (`vault/plans/EZD-205.md`, `vault/plans/EZD-207.md`; `vault/tickets/STATUS.md:179,181`, read 2026-11-05). The logic part needs only EZD-205a/205b contracts; the screen part needs EZD-207a/207b contracts. Each part is planned after the parts it reads, so its interface contract matches real contracts (lesson EZD-025: a plan written before its dependencies split cites their real exports).
- Part a is pure TypeScript with unit tests only; part b is React, canvas wiring and browser tests. Same cut as EZD-209 (`typed-entry.ts` pure, `TypedEntryLayer.tsx` screen).

The work splits into two lettered parts, built a → b. Each part is planned as its own unit from its section here.

### Part EZD-210a · Wall and Room rectangle tool logic
- **Scope (place):** pure modules, no React and no DOM, in `app/src/editor/tools/` (`eslint-rules/boundaries.mjs` `EDITOR_CODE`: "app/src/editor/ is reserved for the store, canvas and tools"). Not in `packages/geometry/`, which holds model geometry re-run on the server (ARCH Folder layout); tool state is screen state. Pattern: P209 `typed-entry.ts` (pure reducer, never throws).
- **Scope (tool definitions):** a `TypedTool` per tool (P209 C7):
  - Wall: P209 `WALL_LENGTH_FIELD` then `TURN_ANGLE_FIELD` (P209 D-Fields: "EZD-210 reuses them");
  - Room rectangle: Width then Depth, both `kind: 'length'`, `lengthKind: 'wall_room'`, `optional: false` (Q-0570: Room rectangle is a wall and room field; Width across the screen, Depth up and down; S03 Tab);
  - rail entries as EZD-012a `RailTool` (`app/src/components/shell/rail-types.ts`): ids `wall` and `room-rect`, shortcuts `W` and `R` (04 Tool rail; Q-0568 "W and R keys fixed until EZD-222"), labels from 04 Tool rail ("Wall", "Room rectangle"), Wall icon `view_column_2` (board S03, `S03Plan.dc.html:63`), Room rectangle icon `rectangle` (Q-0588 (a)).
- **Scope (Wall chain reducer):**
  - Click sets the start; each next point comes from the snapped cursor (P206 `snap`, with `anchor` = the chain's last point and `referenceDirection` = the last wall's direction, P206 seam "EZD-210 Wall tool") or from a typed commit (P209 `TypedValues` `length`, `angle`) turned into a direction by P209 `resolveTurnDirection` (Q-0560; Q-0570: first wall from the page's horizontal, "where the cursor points" means after snapping).
  - Each segment is committed as one wall when it is entered (AC-6: committed walls are kept). New walls are the default wall, status Existing, on the open floor (P203 `createWallData`; Q-0558; P120a M4 makes `Floor 1` for every project).
  - Thickness: `right` while the chain is open, outside the room once it closes (P203 `thicknessSideFor`; Q-0569 (b); 09j Thickness side rows 1–3).
  - The chain closes when a click lands on its start point (endpoint snap) or a committed segment ends within 1/64" of the start (P202 `pointsEqual`; 03g; 09j Closure row 1).
  - It finishes on double-click, or on Enter while the inline box is closed (P209 D-Enter: Enter with the box closed is `handled: false`, so the first Enter commits the typed value and the second finishes; ticket row "Enter twice").
  - Esc mid-chain drops only the segment in progress; Esc with no segment in progress leaves the tool (Q-0568; AC-6). Esc while the box is open is the box's (P209 D-Esc).
  - Refusals: lengths and angles through P201 `parseLength` and P209 `parseTurnAngle` inside the typed reducer; a segment that would be 0" or over 200' is refused (P203 `wallLengthProblem`; Q-0570).
- **Scope (Room rectangle reducer):** click a corner; drag to the opposite corner, or type Width Tab Depth Enter. It grows from the clicked corner toward the cursor, right and down if the cursor has not moved; Width is across the screen, Depth up and down (Q-0570; AC-12). Typed sizes are the inside finished face and the thickness goes outside, so 12' × 10' is 120 SF inside (Q-0559; 09j Typed length to outside size row 1). It writes four closed walls; the room comes from the reconcile step. Part a's plan decides from S03 and 04 whether a second click without a drag sets the opposite corner, or asks a QP.
- **Scope (writing the model):** one function turns a tool's committed walls into P120b `Change[]` (`{ id, value: ObjectValue | null }`, `schemaVersion` = P202/P203 `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` at build time) and appends the room creates, updates and deletes of EZD-205a's reconcile step for the floor. New ids are v4 uuids (`crypto.randomUUID()`; P202 `levelSchema` and fixtures use v4). Part b passes the result to P120b `ModelStore.applyEdit` once per committed segment or rectangle, so the outbox saves it (P120b; AC-5).
- **Scope (gap box model):** a function over the floor's objects lists the gaps to show, from EZD-205b's closure report: chains of three or more walls with a straight-line miss over 1/64" and at most 12" (Q-0562; Q-0568; Q-0569 (c); Q-0570; 09j Closure rows 1–9). Each entry carries the gap point and size text at 1/16" (never 0", Q-0570) and the actions offered: Pick the wall that absorbs it only when a wall of the chain is parallel to the gap, else Keep the room out of square only plus the Q-0569 (c) line (09j Closure row 6). Because it is derived from the walls, the box comes back after a reload (Q-0570).
- **Scope (pick and keep):** a pick-mode reducer (00e Pick mode: the next click on a wall picks it, Esc goes back to the box; S02 Esc; Q-0570). A pick calls EZD-205b's absorb: success gives `Change[]` (with reconcile), a refusal gives a message key per EZD-205b reason (wall across the gap, wall of another room, a wall left at 0" or over 200'; 09j Absorbing rows 3–5; Q-0568; Q-0570). Keep out of square gives the room change with `closureOverride` who = `ModelLoad.viewer.appUserId` (P120b), when = now, gap = the reported vector (Q-0568; P205 part b, whose save route refuses another user's "who").
- **Scope (snap marker model):** maps P206 `SnapResult.kind` (`SNAP_KINDS`) and point to the marker part b draws, `null` when no snap applies (S03 Snap "Snap marker shows snap type"; Q-0563). The marker is a small cobalt shape per kind, no text (Q-0589 (a)): square endpoint, triangle midpoint, short bar wall face, arc with 90° or 45° angle, small cross increment.
- **Done when:** AC-EZD-210-4, AC-EZD-210-6 and AC-EZD-210-12, verbatim, as unit tests. AC-EZD-210-1, -2, -3, -8 and -9 for their logic: a scripted Wall chain typed 12' Enter, then 10', 12' and 10' each with Tab 90 Enter, gives four walls and one room of 120 SF; 12', 10', 12', 9' 11 1/2" gives one gap entry of 1/2" with both actions, and picking the 9' 11 1/2" wall gives 120 SF while a 12' wall gives the across-the-gap message key (09j Closure rows 1–2; Absorbing rows 1, 3). AC-EZD-210-10 for its model: every `SNAP_KINDS` value maps to a marker.
- **Depends on:** from the row: EZD-205 (both parts), EZD-209, EZD-206. Missing from the ticket row: EZD-203 (`createWallData`, `thicknessSideFor`, `wallLengthProblem`; through EZD-205 and EZD-206), EZD-201 (`parseLength`, through EZD-209), EZD-202 (`pointsEqual`, schema; through EZD-203), EZD-120b (`Change`, `ModelStore`, `ModelLoad.viewer`; phase 3, merged before phase 4), EZD-012a (`RailTool`, done).
- **Files (about 12):**
  - `app/src/editor/tools/`: tool definitions, Wall chain reducer, Room rectangle reducer, model changes, gap box model and pick reducer, snap marker model, `index.ts`, each with a test file;
  - `app/src/server/messages/catalogs/en.ts` (field labels Width and Depth, the refusal and Q-0569 (c) texts; section 6 of part a's plan).
  - Part a's plan greps tests that pin the `en` key list or count and names each edit (lesson L-021, L-049).
- **Tests (about 22):** Wall chain: start click, typed length Enter, typed turn 90 / 45 / 0, cursor direction after snap, close by clicking the start, close by typed lengths (09j Closure row 1), double-click finish, Enter-twice finish, Esc drops one segment and keeps committed walls, second Esc leaves the tool, a 0" and a 200' 0 1/16" segment refused (09j Typed lengths rows 13, 16), thickness `right` then outside after closing; Room rectangle: grow right and down with no move, toward the cursor in each quadrant, typed 12' × 10' → four walls and 120 SF, typed 12'6" × 10' → 125 SF (09j Room area row 2; test script step 2), 0" refused; changes: v4 ids, status Existing, current schema version, reconcile appended; gap model: 09j Closure rows 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9; pick: Absorbing rows 1, 3, 5; keep out of square stores who, when, gap; snap marker per kind and `null`.
- **Complexity:** high. Two interaction state machines over geometry with many refusals, writing model data that every later ticket reads (PROCESS.md section 4). Test-author Sonnet 5.5, builder Opus 5.5.
- **security-review: no.** Pure modules; no route, table, policy, permission or money field. The "who" of an override is checked server-side by EZD-205b's save route.
- **Reviewers:** code-reviewer · calc-auditor yes (lengths, areas, gap sizes) · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer no.
- **Visual checklist:** none (no screen).
- **Proposed wording:** expected: the Width and Depth field labels (Q-0570 names them), the absorb refusal texts (09j Absorbing rows 3–5 "Refused with a message"), the Q-0569 (c) line ("fix the walls once move arrives"), in the style of `office.length.refused` (P201 E11).

### Part EZD-210b · Drawing tools on the plan
- **Scope (mount):** a drawing-tools component in `app/src/editor/tools/`, mounted by EZD-120c's `ProjectEditor` (`app/src/editor/ProjectEditor.tsx`, P120c) in the canvas region over the EZD-207a canvas when the session is `ready`. It renders the rail through `EditorFrame`'s `rail` slot with `ToolRail` (EZD-012a; ARCH Editor shell: "a tool appears only when its feature exists"), and mounts P209 `TypedEntryLayer` with the active `TypedTool`, `canEdit`, `lastValues` (the last wall's length, Q-0564) and `getCursor` (P209 section 9 note).
- **Scope (keys):** W and R pick the tool; Esc runs the part-a reducers; keys whose target passes P209 `isTypingTarget` or whose event is `defaultPrevented` are skipped (P209 section 9 note). No Select tool in phase 4, so the second Esc leaves no tool active (Q-0568).
- **Scope (pointer and overlay):** clicks, double-clicks, drags and moves on the canvas feed the part-a reducers in model inches; pan gestures (space-drag, right-drag, two-finger) stay EZD-207a's (S03 Canvas interactions). The rubber-band wall or rectangle and the snap marker redraw per pointer move with no React render (11 rule 4; ARCH Editor shell). The tool sets the EZD-207b hover mode to `off` while drawing and `wall` in pick mode (P207 part b seam; Q-0570). It needs from EZD-207a/207b (see Ledger notes): model ↔ screen transforms and `pixelsPerInch` readable inside a pointer handler (P206 seam), a camera-change callback outside React, the pointer hand-off, and the hover-mode setter.
- **Scope (gap box):** a small box near each gap from part a's gap model (Q-0569, decisions 05: no new board, built from S02 pieces): the red gap pill with its size (board S02 `S02Import.dc.html:71`, text `5/8" gap` there), and the S02 Resolve the gap buttons "Pick the wall that absorbs it" (icon `ads_click`) and "Keep the room out of square" (icon `rotate_right`) (`S02Import.dc.html:98-100`). It follows pan and zoom through the camera callback. Without Edit model the pill shows with no buttons (Q-0570; AC-8). A refused pick shows part a's message (09j Absorbing row 3).
- **Scope (permissions and states):** without Edit model: no rail, no typed bar, no tool keys; canvas, pan, zoom, Fit and hover stay (Q-0568; S03 Permissions; AC-7). While the model loads the tools are disabled (S03 States "Loading"; P207 split note "keep the bar and tools hidden without Edit model and disabled while loading").
- **Scope (icons and text):** `view_column_2` and the `rectangle` icon through the icon pipeline (ARCH Design tokens, fonts and icons: `icons:fetch`, `icons.json`, `icons:build`), checked for the `viewBox="0 -960 960 960"` format at fetch (lesson EZD-103a), with the `HeaderButton.icon.test.tsx` list edit (lesson L-021). `ads_click` and `rotate_right` likewise unless already present. Rail labels and gap texts in `en.ts`.
- **Done when:** AC-EZD-210-5, AC-EZD-210-7 and AC-EZD-210-11, verbatim. AC-EZD-210-1, -2, -3, -8, -9 and -10 on screen: browser tests run the Slice 4 test script steps 2 (R, click, 12'6" Tab 10' Enter → a closed 12'6" × 10' room with its area), 3 (W chain closed on its start → room), 6 (reload keeps walls and room) and 7 (W chain 12', 10', 12', 9' 11 1/2", Enter → the 1/2" gap box; pick the 9' 11 1/2" wall → 120 SF) (PHASES.md Slice 4), plus the snap marker on screen while drawing and the view-only editor showing the gap pill without buttons.
- **Depends on:** EZD-210a, EZD-207a, EZD-207b, EZD-209, EZD-120c. Missing from the ticket row: EZD-207 parts (the canvas; reached through EZD-209), EZD-120c (`ProjectEditor`; phase 3), EZD-010b (icon pipeline, done), EZD-016a (browser harness, for the visual checklist; done).
- **Files (about 16):**
  - `app/src/editor/tools/`: the drawing-tools component and its CSS module, the overlay module, the gap box component and its CSS module, with test files;
  - `app/src/editor/ProjectEditor.tsx` (mount), and the earlier tests that count rail buttons or read canvas-region text (P120c B2, P207 part a's "rail region absent" test; lesson EZD-136 plan-gap: part b's plan greps and names each edit);
  - `app/src/components/icon/icons.json`, the new SVGs, `app/public/icons/sprite.svg`, `icon-names.generated.ts`, `HeaderButton.icon.test.tsx` (test-author edit);
  - `app/src/server/messages/catalogs/en.ts`;
  - one Playwright spec in `app/e2e/`;
  - `docs/architecture.md`: a new `### Drawing tools (EZD-210)` section (where tools live, the overlay rule, the keys).
- **Tests (about 14):** component: rail shows Wall and Room rectangle with W and R for Edit model and nothing without it; W and R keys pick the tool and are ignored in an input; Esc twice leaves the tool; tools disabled while loading; gap box buttons hidden without Edit model; pick mode Esc returns to the box; overlay redraws with 0 React commits across 50 pointer moves; browser: test script steps 2, 3, 6, 7; snap marker visible at a wall endpoint; view-only gap pill without buttons; room label `ROOM 1 · 120 SF` present (part b's plan says how a test reads WebGL text, through the drawing list or a test hook, from EZD-207b's contract).
- **Complexity:** high. Pointer and keyboard wiring onto the WebGL canvas under the no-render rule, with browser tests of the whole drawing flow (PROCESS.md section 4; Slice 4 Risks). Test-author Sonnet 5.5, builder Opus 5.5.
- **security-review: no.** UI only; writes go through EZD-120a's save route, which enforces Edit model on the server (P120a; EZD-102). No new route, table, policy or money field.
- **Reviewers:** code-reviewer · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier yes · security-reviewer no.
- **Visual checklist:** yes, desktop 1600 × 1000. Rows: rail (board S03 rail card 56 px wide, `S03Plan.dc.html:59`; Wall icon `view_column_2`), active tool button (04 Tool rail: cobalt with a white icon), typed bar with the Wall tool (P209 rows), snap marker (Q-0589 (a)), gap box filled and view-only (S02 pill and buttons), room label.
- **Proposed wording:** expected: gap pill text pattern (board S02 `5/8" gap`), any loading or no-tool text not on a board. The rail labels come from 04 Tool rail; the gap buttons from board S02.

### Applies to both parts
- Numbers come from 09j, 03g and the decisions, never from mockup sample data (KNOWN-LIMITS 5): the S02 board's `5/8"` and S03's `KITCHEN · 165 SF` are illustration.
- No undo, delete or move in phase 4 (Q-0564): neither part binds Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Delete or Backspace, though P120b's store has `undo`.
- Room rectangle is on the rail only; the S03 "Wall tool option" placement is not built (Q-0568: "a rail with Wall and Room rectangle").
- Lessons each plan applies: every test row names the wrong implementation it rejects (L-050); empty, over-limit and malformed inputs get rows (L-052); exact test count and titles (L-034); helpers named with their file path (L-043); no test reads a document (L-041); earlier tests that pin the icon list or `en` keys get named edits (L-021, L-049); every visual row gives a number or a named element (L-054); the `EditorFrame` rail markup is read before asserting attributes on it (lesson EZD-026b).

### Ledger notes for the orchestrator
- EZD-221 depends on base `EZD-210`, so it expands to both parts (`vault/tickets/README.md` split rule; KNOWN-LIMITS 9).
- Slice 4 build order (PHASES.md Slice 4) with the EZD-205 and EZD-207 splits: 201, 203, 205a, 205b, 206, 236, 207a, 207b, 207c, 209, 210a, 210b, 221. Plan 205a and 205b before 210a, and 207a and 207b before 210b.
- When EZD-207a and EZD-207b are planned, their planners should give EZD-210b these seams in their section 3 (P206 seam "EZD-210 Wall tool"; P207 part b "EZD-210 sets the canvas hover mode"): model ↔ screen transforms and `pixelsPerInch` readable synchronously in a pointer handler; a camera-change callback that runs outside React; a way for the active tool to receive left click, double-click, drag and move in model inches while pan gestures stay with the canvas; the hover-mode setter and the hovered wall id. If they do not, EZD-210b's plan raises it.
- When EZD-205a and EZD-205b are planned, EZD-210a needs in their section 3: the reconcile function's input and its create, update and delete output; the closure report per chain (closed, gap, open; gap vector, display size, whether a parallel wall exists); absorb's result and refusal reasons; and the keep-out-of-square room change.

## Sources
- Ticket: `phase-02.md:16`; `tickets.json` EZD-210 (`depends_on` EZD-205, EZD-209, EZD-206); PHASES.md Slice 4 (goal, result, Josh's test script steps 2, 3, 6, 7).

- Mockups: `vault/mockups/S03Plan.png` with `html/project/S03Plan.dc.html` (rail `:59-76`, Wall icon `:63`, room label `:121`, no snap marker drawn); `vault/mockups/S02Import.png` with `html/project/S02Import.dc.html` (gap pill `:71`, Resolve the gap `:98-100`).
- Dependency contracts (section 3, or the split proposal where no section 3 exists): P201, P202, P203, P206, P209 (plus its D-Fields, D-Enter, D-Esc, D-Keys rows and section 9 note for EZD-210), P120a (M4 first floor), P120b, P120c, P205 (split), P207 (split), P238.
- Code read 2026-11-05: `app/src/components/shell/rail-types.ts`, `ToolRail.tsx`, `EditorFrame.tsx`, `index.ts`; `app/src/components/icon/icons.json` (no `view_column_2`, `ads_click`, `rotate_right`); `eslint-rules/boundaries.mjs` (`EDITOR_CODE`).
- Reuse: `vault/research/reuse/phases-02-10.md:26` EZD-210 `none`. Research: no report covers this ticket (no retriever dispatched).
- Architecture: Editor shell (EZD-012); Design tokens, fonts and icons

## Open questions
- Q-0588 (was QP-1): The Room rectangle rail button has no icon on any board (S03 "Room rectangle (R) (not in mockup)"; board S03 rail draws Wall as `view_column_2`); options: (a) Material Symbols `rectangle`, (b) `crop_square`, (c) another icon Josh names. Binds part b (and part a's rail entry).
- Q-0589 (was QP-2): S03 says "Snap marker shows snap type" but board S03 draws no snap marker, so its look is undecided; options: (a) a small cobalt shape per kind (square for endpoint, triangle for midpoint, short bar for wall face, arc with "90°" or "45°" for angle, small cross for increment) with no text, (b) a cobalt dot with a short tag naming the kind ("Endpoint", "Midpoint", "Wall face", "90°", "45°", "1/2" step"), (c) the shape and the tag together.
